front: Distinguish between Mismatch Repair (MMR) and the pathway deficient in Xeroderma pigmentosum regarding their primary biological timing.
back: * MMR: Functions primarily during S-phase to correct replication errors. * NER: Functions throughout the cell cycle to repair environmental damage.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: List three characteristic dermatological findings of Xeroderma pigmentosum besides cutaneous malignancies.
back: * 1. Severe photosensitivity (blistering). * 2. Xeroderma (extreme skin dryness). * 3. Lentigines (extensive dark freckling).

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: The subunit of the prokaryotic RNA polymerase holoenzyme that is essential for the recognition of specific promoter sequences is the [___].
back:
• Sigma (σ) factor.
 • Converts core enzyme to holoenzyme.
 • Provides specificity for promoter binding.
 • Released after transcript exceeds 10 nucleotides.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A 35-year-old patient being treated for Tuberculosis presents with orange-colored urine and tears. The drug responsible for this finding inhibits transcription by binding to the [___] subunit of RNA polymerase.
back:
• β (Beta) subunit.
 • Drug: Rifampin.
 • Blocks initiation of transcription.
 • Prevents chain growth beyond three nucleotides.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Describe the formation of the 'Transcription Bubble' during the initiation phase of prokaryotic RNA synthesis.
back:
• RNA polymerase holoenzyme binds to the Pribnow box (-10 sequence).
 • Local melting of ~14 base pairs occurs.
 • Converts closed complex to an open complex.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Contrast the structural requirements of the nascent RNA transcript in Rho-independent versus Rho-dependent termination.
back:
• Rho-independent: Requires a self-complementary GC-rich 'hairpin' and a poly-U tail.
 • Rho-dependent: Requires a C-rich 'rut' (rho utilization) site.
 • Rho-dependent uses ATPase/helicase activity of the Rho factor.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Explain the subunit composition and functional difference between the prokaryotic RNA polymerase 'Core Enzyme' and the 'Holoenzyme'.
back:
• Core: (α2, β, β', Ω); possesses 5′→3′ polymerase activity but lacks specificity.
 • Holoenzyme: Core + σ factor.
 • Holoenzyme is required to identify and bind the promoter.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: The consensus sequence 5′-TATAAT-3′, which serves as the site of initial DNA melting in E. coli, is termed the [___].
back:
• Pribnow box (or -10 sequence).
 • Located 10 bp upstream of start site (+1).
 • Bound by the holoenzyme during initiation.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: In a laboratory setting, Dactinomycin (Actinomycin D) is added to a bacterial culture. Explain why this inhibits the elongation phase of transcription.
back:
• Intercalates between DNA base pairs.
 • Creates a physical obstruction.
 • Prevents the movement of RNA polymerase along the DNA template.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: During the elongation phase, how does prokaryotic RNA polymerase ensure the transcript remains attached to the DNA template?
back:
• Formation of a short DNA-RNA hybrid helix.
 • Polymerase moves processively, acting as its own sliding clamp.
 • Uses ribonucleoside triphosphates (ATP, GTP, CTP, UTP) as substrates.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Distinguish between the specific roles of the β and β' subunits of the bacterial RNA polymerase core enzyme.
back:
• β (Beta): Responsible for the 5′→3′ catalytic polymerase activity.
 • β' (Beta-prime): Facilitates binding to the DNA template.
 • Both are targets for specific inhibitory drugs.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Identify the two main prokaryotic promoter consensus sequences and their approximate locations relative to the transcription start site.
back:
• -35 Sequence: (5′-TTGACA-3′); initial contact point for holoenzyme.
 • -10 Sequence: (5′-TATAAT-3′/Pribnow box); site of DNA unwinding.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Xeroderma pigmentosum is characterized by a primary defect in the [___] repair pathway, which fails to remove UV-induced bulky DNA lesions.
back:
Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER).

*   Failure leads to the accumulation of pyrimidine dimers.
*   Results in high susceptibility to early-onset skin cancers.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: A 5-year-old child presents with extreme photosensitivity, severe freckling in sun-exposed areas, and multiple biopsy-confirmed basal cell carcinomas. Identify the underlying molecular pathology.
back:
Xeroderma Pigmentosum.

*   Inability of skin cells to repair thymine dimers.
*   Caused by mutations in genes encoding XP proteins involved in Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER).

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Explain the role of UV-specific endonucleases in the DNA repair process that is defective in Xeroderma Pigmentosum.
back:
*   They recognize bulky distortions in the DNA helix (e.g., thymine dimers).
*   They catalyze the dual incision of the damaged strand on both the 5' and 3' sides.
*   This allows the removal of the damaged oligonucleotide segment.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: A patient with photosensitivity and skin cancer has a defect in repairing pyrimidine dimers, whereas a patient with hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer has a defect in repairing replication errors. Contrast these two conditions.
back:
*   Xeroderma Pigmentosum: Defective Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER); targets bulky UV-induced damage.
*   Lynch Syndrome (HNPCC): Defective Mismatch Repair (MMR); targets mispaired bases escaping polymerase proofreading.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Specify the characteristic DNA lesion produced by UV radiation and its physiological consequence in a patient with an autosomal recessive mutation in XP genes.
back:
*   Lesion: Pyrimidine (Thymine) dimers.
*   Consequence: Distorted DNA helix that blocks replication and transcription, eventually leading to malignant transformation if not excised.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: In the interpretation of diagnostic data for Xeroderma Pigmentosum, the presence of multiple [___] [___] [___] at a very young age is a hallmark clinical indicator.
back:
Basal cell carcinomas.

*   Squamous cell carcinomas and melanomas are also common.
*   Reflects cumulative unrepaired DNA damage from sunlight.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: A researcher notes that fibroblasts from a patient show zero 'unscheduled DNA synthesis' following exposure to ultraviolet light. Interpret this laboratory finding.
back:
*   Indicates a failure in the Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER) process.
*   The absence of gap-filling (repair synthesis) confirms a defect in the excision-repair machinery common in Xeroderma Pigmentosum.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Describe the mechanism of 'gap filling' and 'sealing' during the repair process that is typically absent in Xeroderma Pigmentosum.
back:
*   Gap Filling: DNA Polymerase (typically epsilon or delta in eukaryotes) uses the undamaged sister strand as a template.
*   Sealing: DNA Ligase forms the final phosphodiester bond to restore strand continuity.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Contrast the genetic markers used in ASO probes to detect Sickle Cell Anemia versus the diagnostic use of NER-protein assays in Xeroderma Pigmentosum.
back:
*   Sickle Cell (ASO): Detects a specific point mutation in the beta-globin gene.
*   XP (NER Assay): Measures the functional ability of the cell to excise UV-induced DNA distortions, identifying heterogeneous protein defects.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Identify the primary environmental trigger and the specific mode of inheritance associated with the pathogenesis of Xeroderma Pigmentosum.
back:
*   Trigger: Ultraviolet (UV) radiation from sunlight.
*   Inheritance: Autosomal recessive.
*   Pathogenesis: Extreme photosensitivity due to lack of genomic maintenance.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: In prokaryotic transcription, the specific subunit of RNA polymerase required to recognize and bind the promoter region is the [___] subunit.
back:
• Sigma (σ) factor.
• Converts core enzyme to holoenzyme.
• Enables specific binding to -10 and -35 sequences.
• Dissociates after the transcript exceeds 10 nucleotides.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A patient diagnosed with Pulmonary Tuberculosis is prescribed Rifampin. This drug inhibits bacterial growth by targeting which specific prokaryotic mechanism?
back:
• Prokaryotic RNA Polymerase.
• Binds to the β (beta) subunit.
• Prevents transcription initiation.
• Inhibits chain growth beyond the first few nucleotides.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Describe the mechanical formation of the transcription bubble during prokaryotic initiation.
back:
• Occurs at the -10 Pribnow box (TATAAT).
• RNA polymerase holoenzyme unwinds ~14 base pairs.
• Converts the closed complex to an open complex.
• Facilitated by the weak AT-rich hydrogen bonds.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Contrast the structural requirements of Rho-independent (intrinsic) termination with Rho-dependent termination in E. coli.
back:
• Rho-independent: Requires a GC-rich hairpin loop followed by a poly-U tail.
• Rho-dependent: Requires Rho protein (ATPase/helicase) binding to a C-rich 'rut' site.
• Rho-independent relies on physical dissociation via weak U-A bonds.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Specify the individual roles of the β and β' subunits within the prokaryotic RNA polymerase core enzyme.
back:
• β subunit: Provides the 5' to 3' catalytic polymerase activity.
• β' subunit: Functions as the primary site for DNA template binding.
• Together with α and ω subunits, they form the core catalytic machinery.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: The two critical consensus sequences found in the prokaryotic promoter that are recognized by the holoenzyme are the -35 sequence and the [___].
back:
• -10 sequence (Pribnow Box).
• Consensus sequence is 5'-TATAAT-3'.
• Site of initial DNA strand separation.
• Located 10 nucleotides upstream of the transcription start site (+1).

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A research study observes an antibiotic that intercalates between DNA bases, preventing the movement of RNA polymerase in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes. Identify this drug and its effect.
back:
• Dactinomycin (Actinomycin D).
• Intercalates into the minor groove of DNA.
• Blocks transcription initiation and elongation.
• Used primarily as an anti-tumor agent.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Explain the process of 'Promoter Clearance' in bacterial transcription.
back:
• RNA chain reaches >10 nucleotides.
• Sigma factor is released from the holoenzyme.
• Core enzyme undergoes a conformational change.
• Polymerase moves processively away from the promoter to begin elongation.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Distinguish between prokaryotic RNA polymerase and DNA polymerase regarding the requirement for a primer.
back:
• RNA Polymerase: De novo synthesis; no primer required.
• DNA Polymerase: Requires a 3'-OH primer (RNA or DNA).
• RNA polymerase can initiate chains by joining two ribonucleoside triphosphates.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Define the significance of a 'polycistronic' transcript in the context of bacterial gene expression.
back:
• Single mRNA encoding multiple different proteins.
• Produced from a single operon (e.g., lac operon).
• Contains multiple start and stop codons.
• Allows coordinate regulation of functionally related genes.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Xeroderma pigmentosum (XP) is a rare autosomal recessive genetic disorder characterized by a primary deficiency in the [___] DNA repair pathway.
back:
• Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER)
• Failure to excise bulky DNA lesions
• Inherited defect in one of several XP proteins (XPA-XPG)

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: A 4-year-old child presents with extreme photosensitivity, severe cutaneous freckling in sun-exposed areas, and a biopsy-confirmed squamous cell carcinoma. State the likely biochemical diagnosis.
back:
• Xeroderma Pigmentosum (XP)
• Underlying defect in repairing UV-induced damage
• High susceptibility to early-onset skin cancers

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Explain the specific mechanism by which ultraviolet (UV) radiation causes DNA damage that remains unrepaired in Xeroderma pigmentosum patients.
back:
• UV light induces covalent pyrimidine (thymine) dimers
• Dimers cause significant structural distortion of the DNA helix
• Defective NER fails to recognize or excise these dimers

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: A patient with Lynch syndrome has a mismatch repair (MMR) defect. Contrast this with the specific defect and type of lesion seen in Xeroderma pigmentosum.
back:
• Lynch Syndrome: MMR defect; targets replication errors (mismatches)
• XP: NER defect; targets bulky helix-distorting lesions (UV dimers)

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: In the context of the Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER) pathway, identify the specific enzymatic action required to remove the damaged segment of DNA.
back:
• UV-specific endonuclease (excinuclease) activity
• Dual nicks on both 5' and 3' sides of the lesion
• Release of a short oligonucleotide containing the dimer

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: The diagnostic laboratory finding in Xeroderma pigmentosum skin fibroblasts involves an inability to perform [___] DNA synthesis following exposure to UV light.
back:
• Unscheduled DNA synthesis (UDS)
• Reflects a failure to fill gaps after excision
• Used as a confirmatory test for XP

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: A patient presents with neurological degeneration and progressive hearing loss alongside severe photosensitivity. Relate these multi-system signs to the cellular pathology of DNA repair.
back:
• Some XP variants involve neuronal DNA damage
• Accumulation of oxidative lesions or UV damage
• Leads to premature cell death in the CNS

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Describe the sequential roles of DNA Polymerase and DNA Ligase in completing the repair of a DNA strand following the excision of a pyrimidine dimer.
back:
• DNA Polymerase: Fills the gap using the sister strand as a template
• DNA Ligase: Seals the final phosphodiester bond to restore continuity

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Distinguish between the localized effects of UV-A versus UV-B radiation in the context of initiating the pathology seen in Xeroderma pigmentosum.
back:
• UV-B is primarily responsible for pyrimidine dimer formation
• XP patients cannot repair this specific bulky damage
• UV-A contributes via oxidative stress and indirect damage

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
coreConcept: Inheritance and Ocular Signs of XP
front: Identify the inheritance pattern of Xeroderma pigmentosum and the primary ocular sign often noted during clinical examination.
back:
• Autosomal Recessive
• Ocular Signs: Severe conjunctivitis, corneal ulceration, and eyelid malignancies

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: The prokaryotic RNA polymerase subunit responsible for recognizing and binding to specific promoter sequences is the [___].
back:
• Sigma (σ) factor
• Converts the core enzyme into the holoenzyme
• Ensures specificity for the -10 (Pribnow box) and -35 sequences

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A patient with tuberculosis is started on Rifampin. This drug inhibits bacterial growth by binding to the [___] subunit of prokaryotic RNA polymerase.
back:
• Beta (β) subunit
• Mechanism: Prevents the initiation of transcription
• Result: Stops chain growth beyond 3 nucleotides

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Explain the role of the Pribnow box (-10 sequence) during the initiation phase of prokaryotic transcription.
back:
• Serves as the site of initial DNA melting (unwinding)
• Converts the closed initiation complex into an open complex (transcription bubble)
• Consensus sequence: 5'-TATAAT-3'

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Contrast the structural requirements for Rho-independent vs. Rho-dependent termination in E. coli.
back:
• Rho-independent: Requires a GC-rich hairpin loop followed by a string of Uracil residues.
• Rho-dependent: Requires Rho factor (hexameric ATPase/helicase) binding to the 'rut' site on RNA.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Specify the required substrates and the directionality of the catalytic activity of prokaryotic RNA polymerase.
back:
• Substrates: Ribonucleoside triphosphates (ATP, GTP, CTP, UTP)
• Direction: 5′ to 3′
• No primer is required for initiation

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: In prokaryotic transcription, the 'Core Enzyme' consists of the subunits [___].
back:
• 2 Alpha (α), 1 Beta (β), 1 Beta-prime (β'), and 1 Omega (ω)
• Function: Carries out 5' to 3' polymerase activity but lacks promoter specificity

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A laboratory mutation in the 'rut' (rho utilization) site of a bacterial operon is identified. Describe the likely effect on mRNA synthesis.
back:
• Failure of Rho-dependent termination
• Production of an abnormally long mRNA transcript
• Disruption of coordinate gene regulation in the operon

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: How does the prokaryotic transcription complex transition from the initiation phase to the elongation phase?
back:
• The transcript must exceed 10 nucleotides in length
• The Sigma (σ) factor is released
• The core enzyme 'clears' the promoter and moves processively along the template

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Distinguish between the template (antisense) strand and the coding (sense) strand during RNA synthesis.
back:
• Template strand: The 3' to 5' DNA strand actually read by RNA polymerase.
• Coding strand: The 5' to 3' DNA strand identical in sequence to the RNA (except U for T).

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Name the antibiotic that inhibits transcription by intercalating between DNA bases, used primarily in tumor chemotherapy.
back:
• Dactinomycin (Actinomycin D)
• Prevents both transcription initiation and elongation
• Targets rapidly proliferating malignant cells

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: The specialized DNA repair pathway responsible for removing bulky pyrimidine dimers is known as [___].
back: Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER).

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: A 5-year-old child presents with severe sunburn after minimal exposure, extensive facial freckling, and a recently identified basal cell carcinoma. This clinical presentation most likely indicates [___].
back: Xeroderma pigmentosum (XP).

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Explain the molecular role of the UV-specific endonuclease (excinuclease) in maintaining genomic integrity.
back:
• Recognizes bulky lesions (e.g., pyrimidine dimers).
• Cleaves the damaged DNA strand on both the 5' and 3' sides of the lesion.
• Excises the short oligonucleotide to allow for gap filling by DNA polymerase.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Contrast the DNA repair defect in Xeroderma pigmentosum with the defect found in Lynch syndrome (HNPCC).
back:
• XP: Defective Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER) of UV-induced bulky dimers.
• Lynch: Defective Mismatch Repair (MMR) of non-bulky replication errors (mismatched bases).

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Identify the primary molecular DNA lesion that remains unrepaired and leads to skin malignancies in Xeroderma pigmentosum.
back:
• Intrastrand pyrimidine (commonly thymine-thymine) dimers.
• These result from covalent joining of adjacent pyrimidines due to ultraviolet (UV) radiation.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: In individuals with Xeroderma pigmentosum, the inheritance of the underlying genetic mutation follows a/an [___] pattern.
back: Autosomal recessive.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: A patient's skin fibroblasts demonstrate an inability to excise bulky DNA adducts following UV exposure. Explain the likely outcome regarding somatic mutations in these cells.
back:
• Stalled replication forks lead to the use of error-prone bypass mechanisms.
• High accumulation of somatic mutations occurs.
• Results in multiple early-onset skin cancers (basal and squamous cell carcinomas).

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Explain why Xeroderma pigmentosum is characterized by photosensitivity, whereas defects in Base Excision Repair (BER) typically are not.
back:
• XP (NER defect) fails to repair bulky dimers caused by sunlight (UV radiation).
• BER primarily targets non-bulky lesions like deaminated bases (e.g., uracil).
• NER is uniquely required for the repair of the specific distortion caused by UV-induced dimers.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Distinguish between the physical effects of pyrimidine dimers and single-base mismatches on the DNA double helix.
back:
• Pyrimidine Dimers: Cause significant structural distortion (bulky lesions) of the helix.
• Single-Base Mismatches: Result in non-bulky, localized pairing errors without major helical distortion.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Name the specific human proteins whose mutations are the most common cause of Xeroderma pigmentosum.
back:
• XP proteins (e.g., XPA through XPG).
• These proteins are essential components of the human Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER) pathway.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: In prokaryotic transcription, the subunit of RNA polymerase responsible for recognizing and binding to the promoter region is the [___].
back:
Sigma (σ) factor.

*   Converts core enzyme to holoenzyme.
*   Provides promoter specificity.
*   Dissociates after the transcript exceeds 10 nucleotides.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A 45-year-old male on antitubercular therapy experiences orange discoloration of urine. The drug responsible inhibits transcription by binding to which specific subunit of bacterial RNA polymerase?
back:
Beta (β) subunit.

*   Drug is Rifampin.
*   Prevents chain growth beyond 3 nucleotides.
*   Specifically inhibits initiation phase.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Describe the conformational transition of the DNA-RNA polymerase complex at the -10 Pribnow box during initiation.
back:
Transition from 'closed' to 'open' complex.

*   Localized melting of ~14 base pairs.
*   Forms a transcription bubble.
*   Occurs at the TATAAT consensus sequence.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Contrast the mechanism of Rho-independent termination with Rho-dependent termination in E. coli.
back:
Rho-independent: Forms a GC-rich hairpin followed by a poly-U tail (weak A-U bonds) to release RNA.
Rho-dependent: Rho protein (ATPase/helicase) binds a C-rich 'rut' site and catches up to paused RNA polymerase.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Explain how Dactinomycin (Actinomycin D) inhibits the elongation phase of transcription in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes.
back:
DNA Intercalation.

*   Inserts between G-C base pairs.
*   Acts as a physical impediment to RNA polymerase.
*   Blocks both initiation and elongation.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: The prokaryotic consensus sequence centered at -35 is 5'-[___]-3', acting as the initial point of contact for the RNA polymerase holoenzyme.
back:
TTGACA.

*   Determines transcription efficiency.
*   Located upstream of the +1 start site.
*   Mutation here reduces transcription rate.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A laboratory strain of E. coli develops a mutation in the 'rut' site of a specific operon. Predict the most likely defect in the synthesis of the resulting mRNA.
back:
Failed Rho-dependent termination.

*   Rho protein cannot bind nascent RNA.
*   Results in abnormally long transcripts.
*   Inability to dissociate the RNA-DNA hybrid.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: How does the prokaryotic RNA polymerase ensure processivity during the elongation phase after the sigma factor dissociates?
back:
Core enzyme acts as its own sliding clamp.

*   Maintains a short DNA-RNA hybrid helix.
*   Synthesizes RNA 5' to 3'.
*   Reads template strand 3' to 5'.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Distinguish between the 'coding strand' and 'template strand' during the transcription of a bacterial gene.
back:
Template strand: Antisense (-) strand read by RNA Pol to guide synthesis.
Coding strand: Sense (+) strand with same sequence as RNA (U replacing T).

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: State the composition of the prokaryotic RNA polymerase core enzyme and identify the subunit responsible for catalytic 5' to 3' polymerase activity.
back:
Composition: 2α, 1β, 1β', 1Ω subunits.
Catalytic Subunit: Beta (β) subunit.

*   α/Ω: Enzyme assembly.
*   β': Template binding.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: The rare genetic condition Xeroderma pigmentosum is fundamentally caused by an inherited deficiency in the [___] pathway, leading to the accumulation of bulky DNA lesions.
back: * Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER) * Responsible for removing UV-induced pyrimidine dimers that distort the DNA helix.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: A 5-year-old child presents with severe photosensitivity and extensive freckling on the face. Molecular analysis confirms a defect in a UV-specific endonuclease. Identify the likely diagnosis.
back: * Xeroderma Pigmentosum (XP) * Results from the inability to excise thymine dimers, causing genomic instability and early skin cancers.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Describe how the repair of bulky pyrimidine dimers in the skin differs from the repair of small, non-bulky base deaminations (like cytosine to uracil).
back: * Bulky (NER): Requires dual incisions by excinucleases to remove an oligonucleotide. * Non-bulky (BER): Uses DNA glycosylases to remove a single abnormal base.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: A pediatric patient presents with extreme photosensitivity and multiple basal cell carcinomas. Contrast the sub-pathway of 'Global Genomic Repair' with 'Transcription-Coupled Repair' in this condition.
back: * Global Genomic: Scans the entire genome for bulky lesions. * Transcription-Coupled: Specifically targets damage that stalls RNA polymerase during active gene transcription.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Identify the enzymatic step following the excision of a DNA lesion in Xeroderma pigmentosum that requires the use of dNTPs to restore the genetic sequence.
back: * Gap-filling (Polymerization) * DNA polymerase uses the undamaged template strand to synthesize the missing segment of DNA.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: In a clinical diagnostic workup, the confirmation of a(n) [___] pattern of inheritance is essential for categorizing a photosensitive patient as having Xeroderma pigmentosum.
back: * Autosomal recessive * Requires the inheritance of two defective alleles, typically with both parents being unaffected carriers.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: A patient's skin fibroblasts show a total failure to perform the dual incision step on sun-damaged DNA strands. Apply this molecular data to predict the long-term clinical outcome for the patient.
back: * Early and numerous skin malignancies * Inability to fix UV damage leads to permanent mutations in tumor suppressor genes.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Contrast the specific molecular target of the repair system deficient in Xeroderma pigmentosum with the target of the Mismatch Repair (MMR) system deficient in Lynch Syndrome.
back: * XP: Targets bulky, helix-distorting pyrimidine dimers (e.g., T-T dimers). * Lynch (MMR): Targets non-bulky base mismatches (e.g., A-G pairing) or small loops.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Trace the physiological loop starting from UV light exposure to the formation of a 'lariat-free' gap during the repair process in a healthy individual.
back: * UV exposure → Pyrimidine dimer formation. * NER initiation → Endonuclease makes 5' and 3' incisions. * Excision → Removal of 11-12 nucleotide segment.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Name the specific structural unit of DNA formed by ultraviolet radiation that accumulates in the epidermal cells of individuals with Xeroderma pigmentosum.
back: * Pyrimidine dimers (Cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers) * Covalent bonds formed between adjacent thymine or cytosine bases on the same strand.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: The prokaryotic RNA polymerase holoenzyme is formed when the core enzyme associates with the [___], which is essential for promoter recognition.
back:
* Sigma factor (̃σ).
* Enables specific binding to promoter consensus sequences (-10 and -35).
* Dissociates from the core enzyme after the transcript exceeds 10 nucleotides.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A 45-year-old patient being treated for tuberculosis presents with orange-colored secretions. The medication responsible inhibits transcription by [___].
back:
* Binding to the β-subunit of prokaryotic RNA polymerase.
* Blocking the exit of the nascent RNA chain.
* Specifically preventing the initiation of transcription.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Explain the molecular mechanism that facilitates the transition from a closed to an open initiation complex in E. coli.
back:
* Holoenzyme binds the -10 Pribnow box.
* Spontaneous melting of ~14 base pairs occurs.
* Creates a transcription bubble, allowing the template strand to be accessed by the β-subunit.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Contrast the structural requirements of the nascent RNA transcript in rho-independent termination versus rho-dependent termination.
back:
* Rho-independent: Requires a GC-rich hairpin loop followed by a poly-U tail.
* Rho-dependent: Requires a C-rich "rut" site (rho utilization site).
* Rho-dependent requires ATP-dependent helicase activity of the rho (ρ) factor.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: State the direction in which RNA polymerase reads the DNA template and the direction in which the new RNA strand is synthesized.
back:
* Reads DNA template: 3' to 5' (Antisense strand).
* Synthesizes RNA: 5' to 3'.
* Uses ribonucleoside triphosphates (rNTPs) as substrates, releasing pyrophosphate.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: The consensus sequence located approximately 10 base pairs upstream of the transcription start site in prokaryotes is known as the [___].
back:
* Pribnow Box (TATAAT).
* Serves as the site for initial DNA unwinding/melting.
* Located within the promoter region of the transcription unit.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A laboratory strain of E. coli exhibits a mutation in the -35 consensus sequence (TTGACA). Predict the effect on the transcription process.
back:
* Reduced initial binding of RNA polymerase holoenzyme.
* Failure to form the closed initiation complex.
* Significant decrease in the frequency of transcription initiation.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Describe how the catalytic subunits β and β' of the prokaryotic RNA polymerase carry out their specific roles during elongation.
back:
* β-subunit: Responsible for 5' to 3' polymerase activity and rNTP binding.
* β'-subunit: Facilitates binding to the DNA template strand.
* Together, they form the catalytic center for phosphodiester bond formation.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Distinguish between the coding (sense) strand and the template (antisense) strand regarding the final RNA transcript sequence.
back:
* Template (Antisense): Complementary and antiparallel to the RNA transcript.
* Coding (Sense): Identical in sequence to the RNA transcript (except T is replaced by U).
* mRNA is always synthesized using the template strand only.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Identify the subunit composition of the prokaryotic RNA polymerase core enzyme and its primary functional limitation.
back:
* Composition: α2, β, β', ω.
* Function: Possesses 5' to 3' polymerase activity.
* Limitation: Lacks specificity and cannot recognize or bind to promoters without sigma factor.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: In prokaryotic transcription, the specific subunit required for the recognition of the promoter region by RNA polymerase is the [___].
back:
• Sigma (σ) factor.
• It converts the core enzyme into the holoenzyme.
• Enables binding to -10 (Pribnow box) and -35 consensus sequences.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A 45-year-old male with pulmonary tuberculosis is started on Rifampin. Describe the specific molecular mechanism by which this drug inhibits bacterial growth.
back:
• Binds to the β-subunit of bacterial RNA polymerase.
• Physically blocks the exit of the nascent RNA chain.
• Inhibits transcription initiation and prevents chain growth beyond a few nucleotides.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Explain the role of the Pribnow box during the initiation phase of prokaryotic transcription.
back:
• Consensus sequence (TATAAT) centered at the -10 position.
• It is the site of initial DNA melting (unwinding).
• Facilitates transition from a closed to an open initiation complex (transcription bubble).

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Contrast the structural requirements of Rho-dependent termination with Rho-independent (intrinsic) termination in E. coli.
back:
• Rho-independent: Requires a G-C rich hairpin loop followed by a poly-U tail.
• Rho-dependent: Requires a C-rich 'rut' site and Rho protein (ATPase/helicase activity).
• Independent relies on sequence symmetry; dependent relies on protein-DNA displacement.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Specify the subunit composition and primary functional roles of the prokaryotic RNA polymerase core enzyme.
back:
• Composition: α₂, β, β', and ω.
• α subunits: Required for enzyme assembly.
• β subunit: Responsible for 5'→3' catalytic polymerase activity.
• β' subunit: Mediates binding to the DNA template.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: The primary transcript in prokaryotes is synthesized in the [___] direction, using the [___] DNA strand as a template.
back:
• 5' to 3' (Synthesis direction).
• 3' to 5' / Template / Antisense strand.
• No primer is required for RNA polymerase to initiate synthesis.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A researcher observes that a bacterial strain fails to initiate transcription despite a functional core RNA polymerase. Analysis shows a mutation in the -35 consensus sequence. What is the significance of this sequence?
back:
• Sequence: 5'-TTGACA-3'.
• Serves as the initial point of contact for the RNA polymerase holoenzyme.
• Mutations here reduce the efficiency of enzyme recruitment and binding.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Describe the process of 'promoter clearance' during the transition from initiation to elongation in prokaryotes.
back:
• Occurs once the RNA transcript exceeds 10 nucleotides in length.
• The Sigma (σ) factor is released from the complex.
• The core enzyme changes conformation to move processively along the template.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Distinguish between the 'coding strand' and the 'template strand' regarding the resulting mRNA sequence.
back:
• Template Strand: Complementary and antiparallel to the RNA.
• Coding Strand: Identical to the RNA sequence (except T instead of U).
• RNA polymerase only reads the template strand (3' to 5').

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Identify the high-energy bond hydrolysis that drives the addition of a ribonucleotide to the growing RNA chain.
back:
• Cleavage of the high-energy phosphate bond in the incoming nucleoside triphosphate (NTP).
• Subsequent hydrolysis of the released pyrophosphate (PPi) to 2 Pi by pyrophosphatase.
• This makes the reaction essentially irreversible.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: In patients with Xeroderma pigmentosum, the primary genetic defect involves an inability to perform [___].
back: Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER). - Specifically fails to remove pyrimidine dimers. - Results from mutations in XP-related genes (XPA-XPG). - Leads to accumulation of DNA damage.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: A 5-year-old child presents with extreme photosensitivity, multiple 'sun-spots,' and a squamous cell carcinoma on the nose. This condition is inherited as [___].
back: Autosomal Recessive. - Inherited when both alleles of a specific repair gene are mutated. - Characterized by high risk of early-onset skin malignancies. - Parents are usually asymptomatic carriers.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Describe how ultraviolet (UV) radiation typically alters DNA structure in individuals who later develop Xeroderma pigmentosum.
back: - Induces covalent bonding between adjacent pyrimidines. - Creates bulky 'pyrimidine dimers' (e.g., thymine dimers). - These lesions distort the double helix. - Dimers block DNA and RNA polymerases.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Contrast the enzymatic approach for repairing pyrimidine dimers in Xeroderma pigmentosum with the repair of deaminated cytosine (uracil) in DNA.
back: - XP (NER): Removes a short oligonucleotide containing the bulky dimer via dual incision. - Uracil (BER): Removes only the abnormal base using DNA glycosylase, then the sugar-phosphate.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Explain why patients with Xeroderma pigmentosum are at a significantly increased risk for multiple types of skin cancers.
back: - Unrepaired pyrimidine dimers lead to permanent mutations. - Accumulated mutations disrupt cell cycle control and tumor suppressor genes. - Results in numerous basal cell and squamous cell carcinomas.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: The specific enzyme class that is primarily deficient or non-functional in the early recognition step of NER in XP patients is the [___].
back: UV-specific endonuclease (Excinuclease). - Cleaves the damaged strand on both sides of the lesion. - Essential for removing DNA adducts and dimers. - In humans, requires multiple XP proteins.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Laboratory analysis of a patient's fibroblasts shows an inability to excise DNA segments containing thymine-thymine cross-links. This is diagnostic for [___].
back: Xeroderma Pigmentosum. - Confirms a defect in the Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER) pathway. - Clinically presents with severe freckling and photophobia. - Requires strict UV protection.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Detail the steps that occur immediately after the UvrABC excinuclease (or human equivalent) successfully removes a damaged DNA segment.
back: - DNA Polymerase (epsilon or delta) fills the resulting gap. - Uses the intact complementary strand as a template. - DNA Ligase seals the remaining nick. - Restores the phosphodiester backbone.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Distinguish between the target of Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER) and Mismatch Repair (MMR).
back: - NER: Targets bulky, helix-distorting lesions (like UV-induced dimers). - MMR: Targets non-bulky replication errors (mismatches) escaped during proofreading. - Defects cause XP and Lynch Syndrome, respectively.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Identify the two sub-pathways of Nucleotide Excision Repair that protect the genome from UV-induced damage.
back: - Global Genomic Repair (GGR): Repairs damage throughout the entire genome. - Transcription-Coupled Repair (TCR): Repairs damage specifically in actively transcribed genes. - Both are often impaired in XP.

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: The specific DNA lesions, typically resulting from ultraviolet (UV) light exposure, that cannot be repaired in individuals with Xeroderma Pigmentosum are [___].
back: * Pyrimidine dimers (specifically thymine-thymine dimers) * Bulky, helix-distorting adducts * Unrepaired lesions lead to high somatic mutation rates

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: A 5-year-old child presents with extreme photosensitivity, severe facial freckling, and multiple basal cell carcinomas. The underlying biochemical failure involves [___].
back: * Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER) * Inability to excise UV-induced DNA damage * Accumulation of mutations in skin cells

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Explain the mechanism of damage recognition in the repair pathway linked to Xeroderma Pigmentosum compared to mismatch repair.
back: * NER proteins recognize bulky structural distortions in the DNA double helix * Mismatch repair (MMR) identifies non-bulky base-pairing errors * XP involves failure at the distortion-recognition step

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Contrast the clinical risks and molecular defects of Xeroderma Pigmentosum with those observed in Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colorectal Cancer (Lynch Syndrome).
back: * XP: NER defect, bulky dimers, high skin cancer risk * Lynch: Mismatch Repair (MMR) defect, replication errors, high colon cancer risk * XP lesions are environmental (UV); Lynch are replication-dependent

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Identify the final enzymatic step required to restore the continuity of the DNA backbone once the gap has been filled in the repair of UV damage.
back: * DNA Ligase * Catalyzes phosphodiester bond formation * Re-joins the repaired patch to the original DNA strand

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Xeroderma Pigmentosum is characterized by an [___] pattern of inheritance.
back: * Autosomal recessive * Requires homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations * High risk in families with consanguinity

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: A laboratory analysis of fibroblasts from a patient with photophobia and skin blistering shows a failure to resume transcription after UV stress. Interpret this finding.
back: * Indicates a defect in Transcription-Coupled Repair (TCR) * A specific sub-pathway of Nucleotide Excision Repair * Pathognomonic for Xeroderma Pigmentosum when combined with clinical signs

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Detail the molecular events of 'excinuclease' activity and how its failure differentiates XP from diseases with single-strand break repair defects.
back: * Excinuclease makes dual incisions on the 5' and 3' sides of a lesion * It removes a bulky oligonucleotide (approx. 30 bases in humans) * XP specifically lacks this dual incision capability for bulky adducts

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: Contrast the enzymatic initiation of Base Excision Repair (BER) with the initiation of the pathway deficient in Xeroderma Pigmentosum.
back: * BER begins with a glycosylase removing a single abnormal base * XP/NER begins with a multi-protein complex recognizing helix distortion * BER handles non-bulky damage; NER handles bulky environmental damage

category: Interpret Xeroderma pigmentosa on basis of sign /symptoms and data
front: List the primary cutaneous signs that characterize the early clinical progression of Xeroderma Pigmentosum after minimal sun exposure.
back: * Severe erythema (sunburn) and blistering * Extensive lentigines (freckle-like spots) * Early onset of actinic keratosis and skin malignancies

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: The [___] subunit of prokaryotic RNA polymerase is responsible for recognizing and binding to the promoter region, converting the core enzyme into a functional holoenzyme.
back: 1. Sigma factor (σ). 2. Provides specificity for promoter recognition. 3. Released from the core enzyme after the transcript exceeds 10 nucleotides in length.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A 35-year-old male with persistent cough and night sweats is started on a multi-drug regimen including Rifampin. Describe the specific biochemical target of this medication.
back: 1. Binds to the β subunit of bacterial RNA polymerase. 2. Inhibits the initiation phase of transcription. 3. Prevents RNA chain growth beyond three nucleotides.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Contrast the distinct roles of the -35 sequence and the Pribnow box during the initiation of prokaryotic transcription.
back: 1. -35 Sequence (TTGACA): Initial contact point for the RNA polymerase holoenzyme. 2. Pribnow Box (-10 sequence): Site where DNA melting occurs to form the open transcription bubble.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A bacterial mutation prevents the formation of GC-rich hairpin structures in nascent RNA. Distinguish which transcription termination mechanism is primarily affected.
back: 1. Rho-independent (intrinsic) termination. 2. Requires a self-complementary GC-rich stem-loop followed by a string of uracil residues to facilitate transcript dissociation.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Identify the specific step of the central dogma inhibited by the anticancer drug Dactinomycin (Actinomycin D).
back: 1. Transcription (initiation and elongation). 2. Mechanism: Intercalates between DNA bases, creating a physical barrier to the movement of RNA polymerase.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: In Escherichia coli transcription, the [___] protein acts as a hexameric ATPase with helicase activity to displace the RNA transcript from its DNA template.
back: 1. Rho (ρ) factor. 2. Binds to C-rich 'rut' sites on the nascent RNA. 3. Uses ATP energy to separate the RNA-DNA hybrid helix.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A researcher identifies an mRNA molecule containing multiple sets of start and stop codons that produces three distinct enzymes. Name this transcript type and its organismal source.
back: 1. Polycistronic mRNA. 2. Characteristic of prokaryotic organisms. 3. Allows for the coordinate regulation of genes within a single operon.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Explain the interaction between Rho factor and RNA polymerase that leads to the termination of transcription.
back: 1. Rho binds the 'rut' site and moves 5' to 3' along the RNA. 2. RNA polymerase pauses at a termination sequence. 3. Rho catches up and uses helicase activity to release the transcript.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Contrast the coordinate regulation of ribosomal proteins (r-proteins) when rRNA levels are high versus when they are critically low in a bacterial cell.
back: 1. High rRNA: r-proteins bind rRNA for ribosome assembly. 2. Low rRNA: Excess r-proteins bind their own polycistronic mRNA at the Shine-Dalgarno sequence, inhibiting further translation.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Identify the specific component of the prokaryotic RNA polymerase core enzyme that possesses 5' to 3' catalytic activity.
back: 1. The β subunit. 2. Core enzyme composition: 2α, 1β, 1β', 1Ω. 3. Function: Catalyzes phosphodiester bond formation using ribonucleoside triphosphates (ATP, UTP, GTP, CTP).

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: The prokaryotic RNA polymerase subunit required for the recognition of specific promoter sequences to initiate transcription is the [___].
back:
• Sigma (σ) factor
• Combines with the core enzyme to form the holoenzyme
• Dissociates after the transcript exceeds 10 nucleotides in length.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A patient diagnosed with Tuberculosis is prescribed Rifampin. Explain the specific molecular mechanism by which this antibiotic arrests bacterial growth.
back:
• Binds to the β-subunit of prokaryotic RNA polymerase
• Inhibits the initiation of transcription
• Prevents RNA chain growth beyond the first few nucleotides.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Describe the formation of the 'transcription bubble' during the initiation phase in E. coli.
back:
• RNA Pol holoenzyme binds the -10 Pribnow box
• Approximately 14 base pairs of DNA are melted (unwound)
• Converts the closed initiation complex into an open complex.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Contrast the 'Core Enzyme' with the 'Holoenzyme' of prokaryotic RNA polymerase regarding composition and function.
back:
• Core Enzyme: α2ββ'Ω; possesses 5'→3' polymerase activity but lacks specificity.
• Holoenzyme: Core + σ factor; essential for specific promoter recognition and initiation.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Identify the two specific consensus sequences found in prokaryotic promoters that facilitate RNA polymerase binding.
back:
• -35 Sequence (5'-TTGACA-3'): Initial contact point for the holoenzyme
• -10 Sequence (5'-TATAAT-3' or Pribnow box): Site of DNA melting.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Rho-independent (intrinsic) termination is finalized when the nascent RNA transcript forms a GC-rich [___] followed by a string of uracil residues.
back:
• Hairpin (or stem-loop) structure
• Uracil-Adenine bonds are weak, facilitating the separation of RNA from the DNA template.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A laboratory mutation results in a bacterial cell lacking Rho (ρ) factor. Predict the impact on the termination of transcription.
back:
• Failure to terminate at 'rut' (rho utilization) sites
• RNA polymerase remains attached to the RNA-DNA hybrid
• Only intrinsic (rho-independent) termination remains functional.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Detail the substrates and directionality of RNA synthesis during the elongation phase in prokaryotes.
back:
• Direction: 5' to 3' (antiparallel to DNA template)
• Substrates: 5'-ribonucleoside triphosphates (ATP, GTP, CTP, UTP)
• Driven by the release and hydrolysis of pyrophosphate (PPi).

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Differentiate between prokaryotic RNA polymerase and DNA polymerase III regarding their proofreading (3'→5' exonuclease) capabilities.
back:
• DNA Polymerase III: Possesses 3'→5' exonuclease activity for high-fidelity replication.
• RNA Polymerase: Lacks a dedicated 3'→5' exonuclease domain, resulting in a higher error rate.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Specify the exact subunit of the prokaryotic RNA polymerase core enzyme responsible for the catalytic 5'→3' polymerase activity.
back:
• The β-subunit
• Forms the phosphodiester bonds between ribonucleotides
• Target of Rifampin inhibition.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: The subunit of prokaryotic RNA polymerase responsible for recognizing and binding to the specific promoter region to form a holoenzyme is the [___].
back:
• Sigma factor (σ).
• Enables specificity for promoter consensus sequences.
• Dissociates after the transcript exceeds 10 nucleotides.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A patient with tuberculosis is treated with Rifampin. This antibiotic exerts its bactericidal effect by targeting which specific component of the prokaryotic transcriptional machinery?
back:
• Target: β (beta) subunit of RNA polymerase.
• Mechanism: Inhibits transcription initiation.
• Prevents chain growth beyond three nucleotides.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Explain the role of the Pribnow box during the initiation phase of prokaryotic transcription.
back:
• Consensus sequence (TATAAT) at -10 position.
• Site of DNA melting (unwinding).
• Facilitates transition from closed to open complex (transcription bubble).

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Contrast the structural requirements of Rho-independent versus Rho-dependent termination in E. coli.
back:
• Rho-independent: GC-rich hairpin (stem-loop) followed by a poly-U tail.
• Rho-dependent: Requires Rho protein (ATPase/helicase) binding to a C-rich 'rut' site.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Identify the energetic driver and the specific directionality of RNA chain growth during prokaryotic elongation.
back:
• Driver: Hydrolysis of pyrophosphate (PPi) from nucleoside triphosphates.
• Direction: 5' to 3' (antiparallel to DNA template).

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: The five peptide subunits (2α, 1β, 1β', 1Ω) that possess 5'→3' polymerase activity but lack promoter specificity are collectively called the [___].
back:
• Core Enzyme.
• β subunit: Catalytic activity.
• β' subunit: Template binding.
• α/Ω subunits: Assembly and stability.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: In a research model, a mutation in the -35 consensus sequence of a bacterial gene is identified. Predict the primary effect on the transcription process.
back:
• Impaired initial binding of the RNA polymerase holoenzyme.
• Decreased frequency of transcription initiation.
• Reduced overall gene expression.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Describe the fate of the Sigma factor once the RNA polymerase begins the elongation phase.
back:
• Released from the holoenzyme.
• Occurs once the transcript is >10 nucleotides long.
• Allows the core enzyme to clear the promoter and become processive.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Distinguish between the coding (sense) strand and the template (antisense) strand during prokaryotic transcription.
back:
• Template Strand: Copied by RNA polymerase (3' to 5' direction).
• Coding Strand: Identical to the RNA transcript (except U replaces T).

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Mention the primary differences between prokaryotic DNA Polymerase and RNA Polymerase regarding primer requirements and proofreading.
back:
• Primer: RNA polymerase does NOT require a primer.
• Proofreading: RNA polymerase lacks 3'→5' exonuclease activity (higher error rate).

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: The [___] factor is the specific auxiliary subunit of the prokaryotic RNA polymerase holoenzyme that enables the recognition of promoter regions on the DNA template.
back:
• Sigma (σ) factor.
• Converts the core enzyme into the holoenzyme.
• Dissociates from the complex after the transcript exceeds 10 nucleotides in length.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A patient with tuberculosis is prescribed Rifampin. This antibiotic exerts its bactericidal effect by binding to the [___] subunit of bacterial RNA polymerase.
back:
• Beta (β) subunit.
• Inhibits the initiation of transcription.
• Prevents the growth of the RNA chain beyond three nucleotides.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Explain the role of the Pribnow box (TATAAT) during the initiation of prokaryotic transcription.
back:
• Located centered at the -10 position of the promoter.
• Serves as the site of initial DNA melting (unwinding).
• Facilitates the conversion of the closed initiation complex to an open complex.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Contrast the structural requirements of Rho-independent termination with the enzymatic activity of Rho-dependent termination in E. coli.
back:
• Rho-independent: Requires a stable GC-rich hairpin (stem-loop) followed by a Poly-U tail.
• Rho-dependent: Requires Rho protein (hexameric ATPase) with helicase activity to displace the RNA from the DNA template.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Identify the subunit composition and functional limitations of the prokaryotic RNA polymerase 'Core Enzyme'.
back:
• Composition: 2 α, 1 β, 1 β', and 1 Ω subunits.
• Function: Responsible for 5'→3' polymerase activity.
• Limitation: Lacks specificity and cannot recognize promoter regions without sigma factor.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: The primary energy source driving the elongation of the RNA chain is the cleavage of high-energy phosphate bonds from [___].
back:
• Ribonucleoside triphosphates (ATP, GTP, CTP, UTP).
• Release of inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi) makes the reaction irreversible.
• Catalyzed by the Beta (β) subunit of the core enzyme.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A laboratory study finds a bacterial mutation in the -35 sequence (TTGACA). Describe the likely impact of this mutation on gene expression.
back:
• Decreased transcription initiation frequency.
• Impairs the initial binding (contact) of the RNA polymerase holoenzyme to the DNA.
• Prevents the formation of the initial closed complex.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Distinguish the orientation of the DNA template strand and the resulting RNA transcript during prokaryotic elongation.
back:
• DNA Template: Read in the 3' → 5' direction.
• RNA Transcript: Synthesized in the 5' → 3' direction.
• Relationship: The two strands are antiparallel and complementary.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Contrast the function of bacterial 'Primase' with that of the standard bacterial 'RNA Polymerase'.
back:
• Primase (DnaG): Specialized monomeric enzyme that synthesizes short RNA primers for DNA replication.
• RNA Polymerase: Multisubunit enzyme that transcribes mRNA, tRNA, and rRNA; does not require a primer.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Define a 'Transcription Unit' as it relates to the prokaryotic primary transcript.
back:
• The DNA segment extending from the promoter to the termination region.
• Encodes a single primary transcript.
• In prokaryotes, this often produces polycistronic mRNA (multiple genes per transcript).

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: In prokaryotic transcription, the specific subunit of RNA polymerase that converts the core enzyme into a holoenzyme by recognizing the promoter region is the [___].
back:
• Sigma (σ) factor.
• It ensures specificity by binding to -10 (Pribnow box) and -35 consensus sequences.
• It dissociates from the core enzyme shortly after initiation.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A patient diagnosed with Tuberculosis is prescribed Rifampin. Describe the biochemical mechanism by which this drug inhibits the causal organism's growth.
back:
• Binds to the β subunit of bacterial RNA polymerase.
• Specifically inhibits the initiation phase of transcription.
• Prevents the formation of the first phosphodiester bond in the RNA chain.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Explain the role of the hairpin loop and poly-U tail in the process of Rho-independent (intrinsic) termination.
back:
• Hairpin: A GC-rich stem-loop structure that slows/pauses RNA polymerase.
• Poly-U tail: Found at the 3' end; its weak U-A bonding to the DNA template facilitates transcript dissociation.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Contrast the functional capabilities of the prokaryotic RNA polymerase core enzyme with those of the holoenzyme.
back:
• Core Enzyme (α2ββ′ω): Possesses 5′ to 3′ polymerase activity but cannot identify promoters.
• Holoenzyme (Core + σ): Competent for site-specific initiation and promoter binding.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Identify the two highly conserved consensus sequences in prokaryotic promoters and their typical locations relative to the transcription start site.
back:
• -10 Sequence (Pribnow box): 5'-TATAAT-3'; the site where DNA melting/unwinding begins.
• -35 Sequence: 5'-TTGACA-3'; the initial contact point for the RNA polymerase holoenzyme.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: During the elongation phase of prokaryotic transcription, the RNA polymerase reads the template strand in the 3' to 5' direction and synthesizes the new RNA transcript in the [___] direction.
back:
• 5' to 3' direction.
• Synthesis is antiparallel to the DNA template (antisense) strand.
• Uses ribonucleoside triphosphates (ATP, GTP, CTP, UTP) as substrates.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A researcher observes that a bacterial cell line fails to terminate transcription of certain genes even after the hairpin loop forms. This likely indicates a defect in the [___] factor.
back:
• Rho (ρ) factor.
• It is a hexameric ATPase with helicase activity.
• It separates the RNA-DNA hybrid at the termination site using ATP energy.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Describe how the "Transcription Bubble" is formed and maintained during prokaryotic elongation.
back:
• RNA polymerase unwinds DNA ahead and rewinds it behind the synthesis site.
• It maintains a localized region of ~14 unwound base pairs.
• A short DNA-RNA hybrid helix (~8-10 bp) is formed within the bubble.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Distinguish between prokaryotic RNA polymerase and DNA polymerase III regarding their requirement for a primer and proofreading ability.
back:
• RNA Polymerase: Does not require a primer; lacks 3' to 5' exonuclease proofreading activity.
