category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Distinguish between the -35 sequence and the -10 sequence regarding their functional roles in initiation.
back: -35 Sequence (TTGACA): Initial point of contact for the RNA polymerase holoenzyme. -10 Sequence (TATAAT): Site where localized DNA unwinding and the transcription bubble form.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Which specific enzyme is responsible for synthesizing the short RNA primers required for DNA replication in prokaryotes?
back: Primase (DnaG). Unlike the standard RNA polymerase, it is a specialized monomeric enzyme. It is required to provide a 3′-OH group for DNA polymerase.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: In prokaryotes, the core RNA polymerase enzyme gains the ability to recognize specific promoter regions only after the binding of the [___] subunit.
back: * Sigma (σ) factor. * Converts core enzyme to holoenzyme. * Ensures specific initiation at the -10 (Pribnow box) and -35 consensus sequences.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A patient with tuberculosis is prescribed Rifampin. This drug acts by binding to the prokaryotic RNA polymerase [___] subunit.
back: * β (beta) subunit. * Mechanism: Inhibits transcription initiation by preventing chain growth beyond 3 nucleotides. * Prevents the transition from initiation to elongation.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Explain the role of the GC-rich hairpin structure in the termination of bacterial transcription.
back: * Forms in the nascent RNA during Rho-independent termination. * Causes RNA polymerase to pause or stall. * Facilitates dissociation of the weak poly-U tail from the DNA template.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Contrast the functional capabilities of the prokaryotic RNA polymerase core enzyme with those of the complete holoenzyme.
back: * Core (α2ββ'Ω): Possesses 5' to 3' polymerase activity but lacks promoter specificity. * Holoenzyme (Core + σ): Capable of site-specific promoter recognition and transcription initiation.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Identify the two highly conserved consensus sequences in a prokaryotic promoter and their significance in initiation.
back: * -35 sequence (TTGACA): Initial point of contact for the RNA polymerase holoenzyme. * -10 Pribnow box (TATAAT): Site where DNA melting and transcription bubble formation occur.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: During prokaryotic transcription, the RNA polymerase reads the DNA template strand in the [___] direction to synthesize RNA in the [___] direction.
back: * Reads template: 3' to 5'. * Synthesizes RNA: 5' to 3'. * RNA is complementary to the template (antisense) and identical to the coding (sense) strand.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A pediatric patient with Wilms tumor receives a drug that intercalates into DNA, blocking all RNA synthesis. Identify the drug and its specific target.
back: * Dactinomycin (Actinomycin D). * Intercalates between DNA bases. * Prevents RNA polymerase from moving along the DNA template, inhibiting both initiation and elongation.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Describe the enzymatic mechanism by which the Rho (ρ) factor facilitates the termination of transcription.
back: * Rho is a hexameric ATPase with helicase activity. * Binds to the C-rich 'rut' site on nascent RNA. * Uses ATP energy to move toward and displace RNA from the DNA template.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Distinguish between prokaryotic RNA polymerase and DNA polymerase III regarding their requirement for a primer.
back: * RNA Polymerase: Does not require a primer to initiate synthesis. * DNA Polymerase III: Requires a short RNA primer with a free 3'-OH group.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Define the term 'polycistronic' and identify the organisms in which this mRNA type is characteristic.
back: * mRNA carrying information for multiple genes grouped in an operon. * Characteristic of prokaryotes. * Allows for coordinate regulation of functionally related enzymes.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
coreConcept: RNA Polymerase Holoenzyme and Sigma Factor
front: The prokaryotic RNA polymerase holoenzyme is formed when the core enzyme associates with the [___] subunit, which is essential for promoter recognition.
back: * σ (sigma) factor. * It provides specificity by recognizing consensus sequences. * It is typically released after the transcript exceeds 10 nucleotides.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A patient diagnosed with tuberculosis is started on Rifampin. This drug's therapeutic effect is mediated by binding to which specific subunit of bacterial RNA polymerase?
back: * β (beta) subunit. * It inhibits the initiation of transcription. * It prevents the addition of the fourth nucleotide in the RNA chain.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Explain the role of the Pribnow box during the initiation phase of bacterial transcription.
back: * Located at the -10 position (TATAAT). * It is the site of localized DNA melting (unwinding). * It converts the closed initiation complex into an open transcription bubble.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Contrast the functional role of the -35 sequence with the -10 sequence (Pribnow box) in a prokaryotic promoter.
back: * -35 Sequence (TTGACA): Initial contact point for the holoenzyme; forms the closed complex. * -10 Sequence (TATAAT): Facilitates strand separation; forms the open complex. * Both are cis-acting regulatory elements.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Identify the enzymatic activity and energy source used by the Rho (ρ) factor to terminate transcription.
back: * Hexameric ATPase with helicase activity. * It uses energy from ATP hydrolysis. * It moves along the RNA to physically separate the RNA-DNA hybrid.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: During the elongation phase, RNA polymerase synthesizes a new transcript in the [___] direction using the DNA template strand.
back: * 5' to 3' direction. * It reads the DNA template in the 3' to 5' direction. * Synthesis is antiparallel to the template strand.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A bacterial mRNA sequence ends with a GC-rich inverted repeat followed by a string of six Uracil residues. Describe the termination mechanism occurring here.
back: * Rho-independent (intrinsic) termination. * The GC-rich hairpin loop causes the polymerase to pause. * Weak U-A hydrogen bonds facilitate the dissociation of the transcript.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Describe the physiological process that marks the transition from the initiation phase to the elongation phase in E. coli.
back: * Promoter clearance occurs once the transcript length reaches ~10 nucleotides. * Sigma (σ) factor is released from the holoenzyme. * The core enzyme remains bound as a sliding clamp to continue synthesis.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Distinguish between the template (antisense) strand and the coding (sense) strand in the context of transcription.
back: * Template: The DNA strand actually read by RNA polymerase (3' to 5'). * Coding: The DNA strand identical to the RNA sequence (except U replaces T); 5' to 3'.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: List the specific polypeptide subunits that comprise the prokaryotic RNA polymerase core enzyme.
back: * Two α (alpha) subunits. * One β (beta) subunit. * One β' (beta prime) subunit. * One Ω (omega) subunit.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: In prokaryotic transcription, the specific subunit required for the RNA polymerase core enzyme to recognize and bind the promoter specifically is the [___].
back:
• Sigma (σ) factor
• It converts the core enzyme into a holoenzyme
• It dissociates after the transcript exceeds 10 nucleotides in length.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A patient diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis is prescribed Rifampin. Describe the specific molecular target and mechanism of action for this antibiotic.
back:
• Target: β-subunit of bacterial RNA polymerase
• Mechanism: Inhibits transcription initiation
• It prevents the exit of the nascent RNA chain, blocking further growth.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Explain the biochemical events that occur during the transition from a 'closed' to an 'open' initiation complex in E. coli.
back:
• RNA polymerase holoenzyme binds to the -35 and -10 promoter sequences
• The -10 region (Pribnow box) undergoes local unwinding (melting)
• A 'transcription bubble' of ~14 base-pairs is formed.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Contrast the structural requirements for Rho-independent (intrinsic) termination versus Rho-dependent termination in prokaryotes.
back:
• Rho-independent: Requires a G-C rich hairpin loop followed by a poly-U (uracil) tail in the RNA
• Rho-dependent: Requires a C-rich 'rut' site and Rho protein (ATPase/helicase activity).

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Specify the substrates and the directionality of chain growth utilized by prokaryotic RNA polymerase during elongation.
back:
• Substrates: Ribonucleoside triphosphates (ATP, GTP, CTP, UTP)
• Direction: 5' → 3' end
• Key Fact: No primer is required for initiation.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: The highly conserved TATAAT sequence, located approximately 10 base pairs upstream of the transcription start site in bacteria, is commonly called the [___].
back:
• Pribnow box
• It is the site where initial DNA melting occurs
• It is a consensus sequence recognized by the sigma factor.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: A researcher observes that a mutated E. coli strain can no longer synthesize mRNA for multiple proteins from a single promoter. Identify the type of mRNA affected.
back:
• Polycistronic mRNA
• Characteristic of prokaryotic operons (e.g., lac operon)
• Allows coordinate regulation of functionally related genes.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Explain the functional difference between the RNA polymerase core enzyme and the holoenzyme in regards to template binding.
back:
• Core Enzyme: Possesses 5' → 3' polymerase activity but binds DNA randomly
• Holoenzyme: (Core + Sigma) specifically recognizes and binds promoter regions.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Contrast prokaryotic RNA polymerase with DNA polymerase III regarding their requirement for a primer and proofreading (exonuclease) activity.
back:
• RNA Pol: No primer required; no 3' → 5' exonuclease activity
• DNA Pol III: Requires RNA primer; has 3' → 5' exonuclease (proofreading) activity.

category: Explain the transcription in prokaryotes focusing on the following key points; RNA polymerase, its components and functions, Initiation, elongation and termination of transcription
front: Identify the antibiotic that inhibits transcription in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes by intercalating between DNA bases.
back:
• Dactinomycin (Actinomycin D)
• Binds to G-C rich regions
• Physically blocks the movement of RNA polymerase during elongation.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: The specific eukaryotic enzyme primarily responsible for the synthesis of precursors for messenger RNA (mRNA) and certain small non-coding RNAs is [___].
back:
• RNA Polymerase II
• Synthesizes hnRNA (pre-mRNA)
• Also produces snoRNA, snRNA, and microRNA
• Highly sensitive to alpha-amanitin inhibition.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A patient presents with severe gastrointestinal distress followed by hepatic failure after ingesting 'death cap' mushrooms. The pathophysiology involves the inhibition of [___] by alpha-amanitin.
back:
• RNA Polymerase II
• Mechanism: Binds the enzyme and slows its movement during transcription
• Result: Failure of mRNA synthesis and subsequent protein production.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Explain the fundamental difference between RNA polymerase and DNA polymerase regarding the requirement for a primer to initiate nucleic acid synthesis.
back:
• DNA Polymerase: Requires a pre-existing RNA primer with a free 3'-OH group.
• RNA Polymerase: Can initiate synthesis de novo without a primer.
• Commonality: Both synthesize in the 5' to 3' direction.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast the spatial and temporal relationship of transcription and translation in prokaryotes versus eukaryotes.
back:
• Prokaryotes: Coupled; translation begins before transcription is complete (no nucleus).
• Eukaryotes: Separated; transcription/processing occurs in the nucleus, while translation occurs in the cytoplasm.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Identify the primary functional distinction between the TATA (Hogness) box and an enhancer in the regulation of eukaryotic transcription.
back:
• TATA Box: Core promoter element; site for assembly of the general transcription initiation complex.
• Enhancer: Distal regulatory element; increases transcription rate by bending DNA to interact with the promoter complex.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: In eukaryotic transcription, the core promoter consensus sequence located approximately 25 nucleotides upstream of the transcription start site is the [___].
back:
• TATA box (Hogness box)
• Recognized by TFIID (specifically TATA-binding protein)
• Determines the precise start site for RNA Polymerase II.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A patient with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) produces autoantibodies against [___], which are ribonucleoprotein particles essential for the splicing of pre-mRNA.
back:
• snRNPs (Small Nuclear Ribonucleoprotein Particles)
• Components: U1, U2, U4, U5, and U6
• Function: Form the spliceosome to remove introns and join exons.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Describe the mechanism by which histone acetylation facilitates the initiation of eukaryotic transcription.
back:
• Enzyme: Histone acetyltransferases (HATs)
• Mechanism: Adds acetyl groups to lysine residues, neutralizing positive charges
• Result: Weakens histone-DNA interaction, allowing transcription factor access.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast the genomic coverage of DNA replication with that of eukaryotic transcription.
back:
• Replication: 'All-or-none' process; copies the entire genome exactly once per cell cycle.
• Transcription: Highly selective; copies only specific genes as needed, often producing multiple transcripts.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: List the three major co-transcriptional modifications required to convert eukaryotic heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA) into mature mRNA.
back:
• 5' Capping: Addition of 7-methylguanosine
• 3' Polyadenylation: Addition of Poly-A tail
• Splicing: Removal of introns and ligation of exons.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: The primary enzyme responsible for synthesizing the nuclear precursors of all eukaryotic messenger RNA (mRNA) is [___].
back:
*   RNA Polymerase II (RNA Pol II).
*   Also synthesizes several small non-coding RNAs like snRNA and miRNA.
*   It is highly sensitive to the toxin alpha-amanitin found in certain mushrooms.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A patient presents with severe gastrointestinal distress and liver failure after consuming wild 'death cap' mushrooms. Identify the specific cellular process and enzyme inhibited by the toxin involved.
back:
*   Condition: Alpha-amanitin poisoning.
*   Mechanism: Inhibition of RNA Polymerase II.
*   Effect: Blocks the synthesis of mRNA, preventing protein production and leading to massive cell death (apoptosis).

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Explain how the covalent modification of histone proteins by Histone Acetyltransferases (HATs) facilitates eukaryotic transcription initiation.
back:
*   HATs add acetyl groups to lysine residues on histone tails.
*   This neutralizes the positive charge of histones, weakening their bond with negatively charged DNA.
*   Result: Chromatin decondenses (euchromatin), allowing transcription factors access to DNA.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast the specific RNA products synthesized by Eukaryotic RNA Polymerases I, II, and III.
back:
*   Pol I: Synthesizes the 28S, 18S, and 5.8S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) in the nucleolus.
*   Pol II: Synthesizes mRNA and microRNA (miRNA).
*   Pol III: Synthesizes transfer RNA (tRNA) and 5S rRNA.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Describe the molecular interaction that allows extracellular signals like glucagon to regulate the transcription of gluconeogenic genes via the cAMP pathway.
back:
*   Glucagon increases intracellular cAMP, activating Protein Kinase A (PKA).
*   PKA phosphorylates CREB (cAMP Response Element-Binding protein).
*   Phosphorylated CREB binds the cAMP Response Element (CRE) on DNA to activate gene expression.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: The unique 5' cap added to eukaryotic pre-mRNA consists of a [___] molecule attached via a rare 5'-to-5' triphosphate linkage.
back:
*   7-methylguanosine.
*   Functions: Protects mRNA from exonuclease degradation.
*   Serves as a recognition signal for the translational machinery to initiate protein synthesis.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A child is diagnosed with beta-thalassemia. Genetic testing reveals a mutation at an intron-exon junction. Explain the molecular defect affecting the mRNA.
back:
*   Defect: Splice site mutation.
*   Mechanism: Prevents proper removal of introns or causes exon skipping.
*   Result: Production of non-functional mRNA and truncated or aberrant beta-globin proteins.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Explain the mechanism of the 'lariat' structure formation during the splicing of eukaryotic pre-mRNA.
back:
*   The 2'-OH group of an internal branch-point Adenosine attacks the 5' splice site.
*   This forms a 2'-5' phosphodiester bond, creating a loop (lariat).
*   The 3'-OH of the upstream exon then joins the downstream exon.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast the genomic organization of prokaryotic mRNA with eukaryotic mRNA regarding the number of genes encoded per transcript.
back:
*   Prokaryotic mRNA: Polycistronic (carries information for multiple related genes in one operon).
*   Eukaryotic mRNA: Monocistronic (carries information for only one gene per transcript).
*   Eukaryotes utilize a nuclear membrane to separate transcription from translation.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Name the specific general transcription factor that contains the TATA-binding protein (TBP) and initiates the assembly of the pre-initiation complex.
back:
*   TFIID.
*   Function: Recognizes the TATA (Hogness) box in the core promoter.
*   Recruits RNA Polymerase II and other general transcription factors (like TFIIB and TFIIF) to the site.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: The eukaryotic enzyme responsible for synthesizing all protein-coding messenger RNA (mRNA) and most snRNA is [___].
back:
• RNA Polymerase II
• It recognizes core promoter elements like the TATA box
• It is highly sensitive to inhibition by alpha-amanitin from poisonous mushrooms.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
coreConcept: Spliceosome Function in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
front: A 25-year-old female presents with a malar rash and joint pain. Lab tests show antibodies against snRNPs (Smith antibodies). Identify the nuclear process directly impaired in this patient.
back:
• Splicing of pre-mRNA
• snRNPs (U1, U2, U4, U5, U6) form the spliceosome
• They remove non-coding introns and join expressed exons together.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Explain the role of the 5' cap and 3' poly-A tail in eukaryotic mRNA maturation.
back:
• Stability: Protects mRNA from nuclease degradation
• Export: Facilitates transport from the nucleus to the cytosol
• Translation: Serves as a recognition signal for ribosomes to initiate protein synthesis.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast the removal of RNA primers between prokaryotic and eukaryotic DNA replication systems.
back:
• Prokaryotes: DNA Polymerase I uses its 5' to 3' exonuclease activity
• Eukaryotes: RNA primers are removed by RNase H and Flap Endonuclease 1 (FEN1).

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: List the specific functions of eukaryotic DNA polymerases delta (δ) and epsilon (ε) during the S-phase of the cell cycle.
back:
• Pol delta (δ): Elongates Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand
• Pol epsilon (ε): Completes DNA synthesis on the leading strand
• Both possess 3' to 5' exonuclease activity for proofreading.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Eukaryotic chromosomes contain multiple [___], which allows for the rapid replication of large genomes compared to the single site found in prokaryotes.
back:
• Origins of Replication
• These sites are often AT-rich to facilitate easier strand separation (melting)
• They generate bidirectional replication forks and multiple replication bubbles.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A patient ingests Death Cap mushrooms (Amanita phalloides). Describe the molecular mechanism of the resulting liver failure.
back:
• Alpha-amanitin binds and inhibits RNA Polymerase II
• This halts the synthesis of mRNA (transcription)
• Protein synthesis ceases, leading to massive hepatocyte necrosis and organ failure.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Describe the mechanism by which enhancers increase the rate of eukaryotic transcription from distant DNA sites.
back:
• DNA looping allows distant enhancers to contact the promoter complex
• They bind specific transcription factors (activators)
• This stabilizes the assembly of the general transcription factor complex and RNA Polymerase II.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast the genetic organization of prokaryotic and eukaryotic mRNA regarding the number of genes they encode.
back:
• Prokaryotes: Polycistronic (one mRNA encodes multiple different proteins)
• Eukaryotes: Monocistronic (one mRNA encodes a single polypeptide)
• Eukaryotic mRNA requires extensive processing (capping, tailing, splicing) unlike prokaryotic mRNA.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Identify the role of telomerase in eukaryotic replication and why it is absent in prokaryotes.
back:
• Function: Maintains linear chromosome ends by adding TTAGGG repeats
• It prevents the 'end-replication problem' and cellular senescence
• Prokaryotes do not need it because their chromosomes are circular.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: In the eukaryotic nucleus, the synthesis of the precursors for messenger RNA (mRNA) and most microRNA (miRNA) is catalyzed by [___].
back:
• RNA Polymerase II
• It recognizes core promoter elements like the TATA box
• Requires General Transcription Factors for recruitment
• Highly sensitive to inhibition by α-amanitin

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A patient presents with severe gastrointestinal distress and liver failure after consuming wild mushrooms. Lab analysis confirms the toxin is inhibiting mRNA synthesis. Identify the specific enzyme targeted.
back:
• RNA Polymerase II
• Toxin: α-amanitin (from Amanita phalloides)
• Prevents the production of functional transcripts
• Leads to widespread cell death, especially in hepatocytes

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Explain how RNA primers are removed during eukaryotic DNA replication compared to the process used in prokaryotes.
back:
• Eukaryotes: Removed by RNase H and Flap Endonuclease 1 (FEN1)
• Prokaryotes: Removed by the 5'→3' exonuclease activity of DNA Polymerase I
• Both allow subsequent gap filling and ligation

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast the roles of DNA Polymerase ε and DNA Polymerase δ during the elongation phase of eukaryotic replication.
back:
• DNA Polymerase ε: Synthesizes the leading strand continuously
• DNA Polymerase δ: Elongates Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand
• Both polymerases possess 3'→5' exonuclease activity for proofreading

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Name the specific consensus sequence located 25 nucleotides upstream of the transcription start site in eukaryotic protein-coding genes.
back:
• TATA Box (Hogness Box)
• Sequence: 5'-TATAAA-3'
• Serves as the cis-acting element for TFIID binding
• Facilitates the assembly of the preinitiation complex

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Unlike prokaryotic DNA replication which starts at a single unique sequence (oriC), eukaryotic replication occurs at [___].
back:
• Multiple origins of replication
• Necessary due to the immense length of eukaryotic chromosomes
• Synchronized to the S-phase of the cell cycle
• Each origin generates a bidirectional replication bubble

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Genetic analysis of a patient with a rare protein deficiency reveals a mutation in the TATA box sequence. Describe the primary effect on transcription.
back:
• Impaired initiation of transcription
• Prevents recognition of the promoter by TFIID
• Results in failure to form the transcription initiation complex
• Leads to a clinical deficiency of the gene product

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Explain the mechanism by which distal enhancer sequences stimulate transcription despite being located thousands of base pairs away.
back:
• DNA Looping: Brings specific transcription factors near the promoter
• Activators: Bind enhancers and interact with the Mediator complex
• Recruitment: Increases the frequency of RNA Polymerase II binding
• Operates independently of orientation or distance

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast the protein component responsible for high processivity in eukaryotic DNA replication with its functional equivalent in prokaryotes.
back:
• Eukaryotes: Proliferating Cell Nuclear Antigen (PCNA)
• Prokaryotes: β-subunit (sliding clamp) of DNA Polymerase III
• Both form a ring-shaped clamp that encircles DNA
• Prevents the polymerase from dissociating from the template

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Identify the general transcription factor (GTF) that initiates the assembly of the preinitiation complex by recognizing the TATA box.
back:
• TFIID
• Contains TATA-binding protein (TBP) and TAFs
• Required for the subsequent recruitment of RNA Polymerase II
• Directs the polymerase to the correct transcription start site

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: In eukaryotic transcription, the specific general transcription factor that recognizes and binds to the TATA box sequence or other core promoter elements to initiate assembly is [___].
back:
* TFIID (specifically TATA-binding protein).
* Essential for recruiting RNA Polymerase II.
* Coordinates the assembly of the preinitiation complex.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A patient presents with severe gastrointestinal distress and liver failure after consuming wild mushrooms. The toxin α-amanitin inhibits which specific enzyme, preventing the synthesis of mRNA?
back:
* RNA Polymerase II.
* Halts the production of messenger RNA.
* Leads to cell death and organ failure.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Explain the role of the eukaryotic Proliferating Cell Nuclear Antigen (PCNA) during the elongation phase of DNA replication.
back:
* Acts as a sliding DNA clamp.
* Ensures high processivity of polymerases.
* Encircles the DNA template to prevent dissociation.
* Functionally analogous to the prokaryotic β-subunit.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast the genomic initiation sites used during DNA replication in prokaryotes versus eukaryotes.
back:
* Prokaryotes: Utilize a single, unique origin (oriC).
* Eukaryotes: Utilize multiple origins per chromosome.
* Essential for replicating massive linear genomes efficiently.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: How do histone acetyltransferases (HATs) facilitate the initiation of eukaryotic transcription?
back:
* Acetylate lysine residues on histone tails.
* Neutralize positive charges to relax histone-DNA binding.
* Facilitate transition from heterochromatin to euchromatin.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: In eukaryotic DNA replication, the RNA primers are excised from the lagging strand by the combined action of RNase H and [___].
back:
* Flap endonuclease 1 (FEN1).
* Replaces the function of prokaryotic DNA Polymerase I.
* Essential for processing Okazaki fragments.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A researcher observes that certain human stem cells do not undergo senescence after multiple divisions. This longevity is primarily attributed to the activity of [___].
back:
* Telomerase (a ribonucleoprotein).
* Maintains chromosome length by extending 3' ends.
* Prevents loss of genetic material during replication.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Describe the mechanism and purpose of the 'scanning' process performed by the 40S ribosomal subunit in eukaryotes.
back:
* Small subunit binds the 5' cap.
* Moves 5' to 3' to locate the start codon.
* Requires ATP and initiation factors (eIF-4 family).

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Distinguish between eukaryotic DNA Polymerase epsilon (ε) and Polymerase delta (δ) regarding their primary roles in the replication fork.
back:
* Polymerase ε: Synthesizes the leading strand continuously.
* Polymerase δ: Elongates Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand.
* Both provide 3' to 5' proofreading exonuclease activity.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Identify the specific eukaryotic RNA polymerase responsible for the synthesis of transfer RNA (tRNA) and the 5S ribosomal RNA.
back:
* RNA Polymerase III.
* Located in the nucleus.
* Transcribes specialized small non-coding RNA molecules.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: In eukaryotic transcription, the specific enzyme responsible for synthesizing messenger RNA (mRNA) precursors and most microRNA (miRNA) is [___].
back:
* RNA Polymerase II
* Primarily synthesizes heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA)
* Highly sensitive to inhibition by alpha-amanitin from poisonous mushrooms

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A 35-year-old patient presents with severe gastrointestinal distress and jaundice after foraging for wild mushrooms. Biochemical analysis reveals systemic inhibition of mRNA synthesis. Identify the most likely molecular target.
back:
* Eukaryotic RNA Polymerase II
* Targeted by alpha-amanitin (Amanita phalloides)
* Halts transcription elongation, leading to liver failure and cell death

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Describe the specific role of the General Transcription Factor IID (TFIID) in the initiation of eukaryotic protein-coding gene expression.
back:
* Recognizes and binds the TATA (Hogness) box
* Contains TATA-binding protein (TBP)
* Coordinates the assembly of the pre-initiation complex and recruits RNA Pol II

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast the spatial and numerical characteristics of DNA replication initiation between prokaryotic and eukaryotic chromosomes.
back:
* Prokaryotes: Single unique origin (oriC) per circular chromosome
* Eukaryotes: Multiple origins per linear chromosome for rapid replication
* Both utilize AT-rich consensus sequences to facilitate initial melting

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Identify the eukaryotic functional counterparts to the prokaryotic DNA Polymerase III regarding leading and lagging strand synthesis.
back:
* DNA Polymerase epsilon: Synthesizes the leading strand
* DNA Polymerase delta: Synthesizes the lagging strand (Okazaki fragments)
* Both utilize 3' to 5' exonuclease activity for proofreading

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: The eukaryotic core promoter consensus sequence (TATAAA), typically found 25 nucleotides upstream of the transcription start site, is known as the [___].
back:
* TATA box (or Hogness box)
* Serves as the primary binding site for TFIID
* Functional equivalent of the prokaryotic Pribnow box (-10 sequence)

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A biopsy of a malignant tumor shows cells with exceptionally stable chromosomal ends despite rapid proliferation. Explain the molecular basis of this finding.
back:
* Upregulation of Telomerase
* Ribonucleoprotein that functions as a reverse transcriptase
* Uses an internal RNA template to extend the 3' G-rich strand

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Explain the mechanism by which enhancers increase the rate of eukaryotic transcription despite being located thousands of base pairs away from the promoter.
back:
* DNA looping allows contact between distal enhancers and the promoter
* Transcription factors bind enhancers and interact with the Mediator complex
* Facilitates recruitment of the basal transcription machinery

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Distinguish between the primary products synthesized by eukaryotic RNA Polymerase I and RNA Polymerase III.
back:
* RNA Pol I: Synthesizes 28S, 18S, and 5.8S ribosomal RNA (rRNA)
* RNA Pol III: Synthesizes transfer RNA (tRNA) and 5S rRNA
* Transcription occurs in the nucleolus for Pol I

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Specify the eukaryotic protein that functions as the sliding clamp for DNA polymerase, and name its prokaryotic structural equivalent.
back:
* PCNA (Proliferating Cell Nuclear Antigen)
* Prokaryotic equivalent: Beta-subunit ring of DNA Polymerase III
* Function: Increases processivity by preventing polymerase dissociation

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: In eukaryotic cells, the specific enzyme responsible for synthesizing the precursor of the 28S, 18S, and 5.8S ribosomal RNA in the nucleolus is [___].
back:
- RNA Polymerase I
- Located in the nucleolus
- Produces most rRNA components of the ribosome

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A patient presents with severe liver failure after consuming the 'death cap' mushroom. This toxicity is due to α-amanitin, which specifically inhibits [___].
back:
- RNA Polymerase II
- Blocks mRNA synthesis
- Slows down the elongation phase of transcription

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Explain how the general transcription factor TFIID facilitates the initiation of eukaryotic transcription at the promoter.
back:
- Recognizes and binds the TATA box
- Contains TATA-binding protein (TBP)
- Serves as the initial scaffold for other transcription factors

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast the eukaryotic Hogness box with the prokaryotic Pribnow box regarding their consensus sequences and relative locations.
back:
- Hogness (Eukaryotes): TATA(A/T)A sequence at -25
- Pribnow (Prokaryotes): TATAAT sequence at -10
- Both function as RNA polymerase recognition sites

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Describe the effect of histone acetylation on chromatin structure and the resulting impact on gene expression.
back:
- Mediated by Histone Acetyltransferases (HATs)
- Neutralizes positive charges on lysine residues
- Relaxes chromatin (euchromatin) to increase transcriptional access

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Transfer RNA (tRNA) and the 5S ribosomal RNA species in eukaryotic cells are synthesized by the enzyme [___].
back:
- RNA Polymerase III
- Synthesizes small non-coding RNAs
- Also produces some snRNA and snoRNA

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A researcher identifies a mutation in a distal DNA sequence thousands of base pairs away from a gene that severely reduces its transcription rate. Identify this cis-acting element.
back:
- Enhancer
- Binds specific transcription factors (activators)
- DNA looping brings the enhancer to the promoter

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Compare the requirement for a primer in eukaryotic DNA replication versus eukaryotic transcription.
back:
- Replication: Requires an RNA primer (via Pol alpha)
- Transcription: No primer required (initiation is de novo)
- Both synthesize nucleic acids in the 5' to 3' direction

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast eukaryotic mRNA with prokaryotic mRNA regarding the number of protein-coding regions contained per transcript.
back:
- Eukaryotes: Monocistronic (one gene per mRNA)
- Prokaryotes: Polycistronic (multiple genes per operon)
- Eukaryotic mRNA requires post-transcriptional capping and tailing

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Identify the general transcription factor (GTF) that provides the helicase activity necessary to melt the DNA double helix during the formation of the preinitiation complex.
back:
- TFIIH
- Possesses helicase and kinase activities
- Phosphorylates RNA Pol II to facilitate promoter clearance

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: The primary eukaryotic enzyme responsible for synthesizing messenger RNA (mRNA) and various non-coding RNAs like miRNA is [___].
back:
• RNA Polymerase II
• Synthesizes mRNA precursors (hnRNA)
• Targeted by the toxin α-amanitin found in certain poisonous mushrooms
• Requires general transcription factors for promoter recognition.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A child with β-thalassemia is found to have a mutation at an intron-exon junction. Identify the molecular process disrupted and its effect on the resulting mRNA.
back:
• Process: RNA Splicing
• Mechanism: Mutation disrupts splice donor/acceptor sites
• Consequence: Causes exon skipping or intron retention, leading to non-functional globin protein and microcytic anemia.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism and significance of the 5' capping process in eukaryotic mRNA synthesis.
back:
• Mechanism: Addition of 7-methylguanosine via an unusual 5'-to-5' triphosphate linkage
• Significance: Protects mRNA from nuclease degradation and serves as a recognition signal for the translation machinery.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast the replication machinery of prokaryotes and eukaryotes regarding the number of origins and the enzymes used for RNA primer removal.
back:
• Origins: Prokaryotes have a single origin (oriC); eukaryotes utilize multiple origins per chromosome.
• Primer Removal: Prokaryotes use DNA Polymerase I (5'→3' exonuclease); eukaryotes use RNase H and Flap Endonuclease 1 (FEN1).

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: How do distal regulatory elements known as enhancers increase the rate of eukaryotic transcription initiation?
back:
• Bind specific transcription factors (activators)
• DNA looping brings activators into contact with the promoter complex
• Can act over long distances, either upstream or downstream of the target gene.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: In eukaryotic mRNA processing, the polyadenylation signal sequence [___] triggers the addition of a 3' tail to stabilize the transcript.
back:
• AAUAAA
• Recognized by an endonuclease that cleaves the pre-mRNA
• Polyadenylate polymerase adds 40–250 adenine nucleotides
• Facilitates nuclear export and increases translation efficiency.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A 30-year-old female with a malar rash and joint pain has anti-Smith antibodies targeting snRNPs. Apply your knowledge to explain the role of these particles in gene expression.
back:
• Component of the spliceosome
• Mediate the removal of introns from primary transcripts (hnRNA)
• Facilitate the precise ligation of exons to form mature, coding mRNA.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Compare the roles of TFIID and TFIIH during the formation of the eukaryotic transcription preinitiation complex.
back:
• TFIID: Recognizes and binds the TATA box via TATA-binding protein (TBP)
• TFIIH: Acts as a helicase to melt DNA and a kinase to phosphorylate RNA Polymerase II for promoter clearance.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Differentiate between the structural and functional outcomes of histone acetylation versus deacetylation in chromatin remodeling.
back:
• Acetylation: (HATs) Neutralizes positive charges on lysine; relaxes chromatin (euchromatin) to stimulate transcription
• Deacetylation: (HDACs) Restores positive charges; condenses chromatin (heterochromatin) to silence gene expression.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Identify the primary structural difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic mRNA regarding the number of protein-coding regions per transcript.
back:
• Eukaryotes: Monocistronic (one mRNA codes for one polypeptide)
• Prokaryotes: Often polycistronic (one mRNA codes for multiple related proteins, as seen in operons).

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: In eukaryotic gene expression, the specific enzyme responsible for the synthesis of all protein-coding mRNA precursors is [___].
back:
RNA Polymerase II. 
- Located in the nucleus. 
- Produces heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA/pre-mRNA). 
- Also synthesizes most snRNA and microRNA (miRNA).

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A 40-year-old presents with severe abdominal pain and jaundice after consuming wild mushrooms. The toxin involved halts protein synthesis by specifically inhibiting [___].
back:
RNA Polymerase II. 
- Toxin: Alpha-amanitin (from Amanita phalloides). 
- Mechanism: Binds Pol II tightly, preventing mRNA synthesis. 
- Clinical Result: Massive hepatocyte necrosis and liver failure.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Explain the role of the General Transcription Factor TFIID during the initiation of eukaryotic transcription.
back:
TFIID initiates assembly of the pre-initiation complex. 
- Contains TATA-binding protein (TBP). 
- Recognizes and binds the TATA box (Hogness box). 
- Recruits RNA Pol II and other transcription factors (TFIIA, TFIIB).

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast the genomic sites where DNA replication begins in prokaryotic versus eukaryotic organisms.
back:
Prokaryotes have a single origin (oriC) on a circular chromosome. 
- Eukaryotes use multiple origins of replication per linear chromosome. 
- Allows rapid replication of massive genomes during S-phase.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: State the structural composition and functional significance of the 5' cap added to eukaryotic mRNA.
back:
7-methylguanosine linked via a 5'-to-5' triphosphate bond. 
- Protects mRNA from 5' exonuclease degradation. 
- Facilitates nuclear export. 
- Required for ribosomal recognition during translation initiation.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: The ribonucleoprotein complex that maintains chromosomal integrity by extending the 3' ends of linear eukaryotic DNA is [___].
back:
Telomerase. 
- Contains a reverse transcriptase (TERT) and RNA template (TERC). 
- Prevents the 'end-replication problem' and senescence. 
- Highly active in germ, stem, and cancer cells.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A patient with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) produces antibodies against snRNPs. These proteins are structural components of the complex that performs [___].
back:
Splicing (Spliceosome). 
- snRNPs (U1, U2, U4, U5, U6) recognize intron boundaries. 
- Removes non-coding introns. 
- Joins coding exons to form mature, monocistronic mRNA.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Detail the difference in enzymatic machinery used for RNA primer removal between E. coli and eukaryotic cells.
back:
E. coli uses DNA Polymerase I (5' to 3' exonuclease activity). 
- Eukaryotes use RNase H and Flap Endonuclease 1 (FEN1). 
- RNase H degrades RNA; FEN1 removes the displaced flap.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Distinguish the roles of eukaryotic DNA Polymerase Delta and Polymerase Epsilon during the S-phase of the cell cycle.
back:
Pol Epsilon: Synthesizes the leading strand continuously. 
- Pol Delta: Elongates Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand. 
- Both possess 3' to 5' exonuclease activity for proofreading.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Identify the primary transcription product of RNA Polymerase I and its cellular location.
back:
Pre-ribosomal RNA (45S pre-rRNA). 
- Synthesized in the nucleolus. 
- Cleaved and processed into 18S, 28S, and 5.8S rRNA subunits. 
- Does not synthesize 5S rRNA.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: In eukaryotic cells, the specific enzyme responsible for synthesizing the precursors for messenger RNA (mRNA) and most microRNA is [___].
back:
• RNA Polymerase II
• Occurs in the nucleus
• Requires general transcription factors for promoter binding
• Highly sensitive to alpha-amanitin inhibition

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A patient consumes wild mushrooms and develops severe hepatic failure. The toxin involved inhibits an enzyme that synthesizes mRNA. Identify the toxin and its specific molecular target.
back:
• Alpha-amanitin (from Amanita phalloides)
• Targets RNA Polymerase II
• Blocks mRNA synthesis and translocation
• Leads to decreased protein production and cell death

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Describe the functional role of the 7-methylguanosine cap added to the 5' end of eukaryotic pre-mRNA.
back:
• Stabilizes mRNA against nuclease degradation
• Facilitates nuclear export of mature mRNA
• Serves as a recognition signal for translation initiation factors
• Added co-transcriptionally in the nucleus

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast the genomic organization of prokaryotic and eukaryotic mRNA in terms of the number of genes encoded per transcript.
back:
• Prokaryotes: Polycistronic (one mRNA encodes multiple related proteins)
• Eukaryotes: Monocistronic (one mRNA encodes a single polypeptide)
• Eukaryotes require separate promoters for each gene product

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Identify the primary mechanism by which a single eukaryotic gene can produce multiple different protein isoforms in various tissues.
back:
• Alternative Splicing
• Differential inclusion or exclusion of specific exons
• Controlled by tissue-specific splicing factors
• Increases proteomic diversity without increasing genome size

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: During eukaryotic transcription, the DNA sequence TATAAA, found ~25 base pairs upstream of the start site, is known as the [___] box.
back:
• TATA (Hogness) Box
• A core promoter element
• Bound by TATA-binding protein (TBP), part of TFIID
• Equivalent to the prokaryotic Pribnow box (-10 sequence)

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A child is diagnosed with β-thalassemia. Genetic testing reveals a mutation in the β-globin gene that creates a new G-U sequence within an exon. Explain the likely molecular consequence for the mRNA.
back:
• Activation of a cryptic splice site
• Results in improper intron removal or exon skipping
• Produces an aberrant, non-functional mRNA transcript
• Leads to deficient β-globin protein synthesis

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Explain how histone acetylation facilitates the initiation of eukaryotic transcription.
back:
• Mediated by Histone Acetyltransferases (HATs)
• Neutralizes positive charges on lysine residues
• Weakens DNA-histone interaction, creating euchromatin
• Increases accessibility for transcription factors and RNA Polymerase

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Distinguish between the roles of the prokaryotic Sigma factor and eukaryotic General Transcription Factors (GTFs).
back:
• Sigma Factor: Single subunit that confers promoter specificity to core RNA Pol
• GTFs: Multiple proteins (TFIID, TFIIB, etc.) required for Pol II recruitment
• Both are trans-acting factors essential for initiation

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Identify the non-templated sequence added to the 3' end of eukaryotic mRNA to enhance stability and translation.
back:
• Poly-A Tail (Polyadenylation)
• Added by Polyadenylate Polymerase using ATP
• Not encoded in the DNA template
• Facilitates translation and protects against 3' exonucleases

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: In eukaryotic transcription, the specific enzyme responsible for the synthesis of messenger RNA (mRNA) and microRNA (miRNA) is [___].
back:
• RNA Polymerase II
• Located in the nucleoplasm
• Specifically sensitive to alpha-amanitin inhibition

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A patient presents with fulminant hepatic failure after consuming wild mushrooms. The toxin involved inhibits eukaryotic gene expression by binding to [___].
back:
• RNA Polymerase II
• Halts mRNA synthesis
• Prevents translocation of the enzyme along the DNA template

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Describe the assembly mechanism of the transcription initiation complex at a eukaryotic TATA-box promoter.
back:
• TFIID (via TATA-binding protein) recognizes and binds the TATA box
• Recruitment of RNA Polymerase II and other GTFs (TFIIA-H)
• Formation of the pre-initiation complex (PIC)

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast the spatial and temporal relationship of transcription and translation in prokaryotes versus eukaryotes.
back:
• Prokaryotes: Coupled; translation starts before transcription finishes (no nucleus)
• Eukaryotes: Separated; transcription occurs in nucleus, translation in cytoplasm

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Explain the fundamental difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic mRNA in terms of the number of genes encoded per transcript.
back:
• Prokaryotes: Polycistronic (encodes multiple related proteins/operons)
• Eukaryotes: Monocistronic (one gene per mRNA molecule)

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: During eukaryotic DNA replication, the initial synthesis of a short RNA-DNA hybrid primer is performed by [___].
back:
• DNA Polymerase alpha (Pol α)
• Contains both primase and polymerase activity
• Lacks 3' to 5' proofreading activity

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A mutation in the beta-globin gene creates a new AG sequence within an intron, leading to aberrant protein production. This clinical finding is due to a defect in [___].
back:
• Splicing (Splice site recognition)
• Activates cryptic splice sites
• Leads to retention of introns or exon skipping

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: How does the eukaryotic cell maintain chromosomal length during replication of linear DNA molecules?
back:
• Telomerase activity
• Uses an internal RNA template to extend the 3' G-rich strand
• Prevents loss of genetic info at chromosomal ends

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast the enzymes used for RNA primer removal in E. coli with those used in human cells.
back:
• E. coli: DNA Polymerase I (5'→3' exonuclease)
• Human: RNase H and Flap Endonuclease 1 (FEN1)

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Identify the distal cis-acting DNA sequences that can increase transcription rates regardless of their orientation or distance from the promoter.
back:
• Enhancers
• Bind specific transcription factors (activators)
• Interact with the promoter via DNA looping

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: The potent toxin ̑̑-amanitin, derived from the "death cap" mushroom, exerts its lethal effect by tightly binding to and inhibiting [___].
back:
* RNA Polymerase II
* Prevents synthesis of mRNA
* Inhibits the elongation phase of transcription
* Halts protein production in the cell

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A 28-year-old female presents with a malar rash and joint pain. Laboratory tests show antibodies against small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs). Identify the specific nuclear process impaired by these antibodies.
back:
* Splicing of pre-mRNA
* snRNPs (U1, U2, U4, U5, U6) form the spliceosome
* Intron removal and exon joining
* Common in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Explain the dual enzymatic roles of the General Transcription Factor TFIIH during the initiation of eukaryotic transcription.
back:
* Helicase activity: Melts/unwinds DNA at the promoter
* Kinase activity: Phosphorylates RNA Polymerase II
* Essential for promoter clearance and transition to elongation

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
coreConcept: Primer Requirements in Replication vs. Transcription
front: Contrast the requirement for a primer between eukaryotic DNA replication and eukaryotic RNA transcription.
back:
* Replication: Requires an RNA primer synthesized by Pol ̑̑/primase
* Transcription: RNA Polymerases initiate synthesis de novo without a primer
* DNA Pols require a free 3'-OH; RNA Pols do not

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Specify the chemical nature of the 5' cap added to eukaryotic pre-mRNA and the donor molecule for its methylation.
back:
* 7-methylguanosine cap
* Joined via an unusual 5'-to-5' triphosphate linkage
* S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) is the methyl donor
* Stabilizes mRNA and initiates translation

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: In eukaryotic promoters, the TATA (Hogness) box is a core cis-acting element typically located approximately [___] nucleotides upstream of the transcription start site.
back:
* -25 nucleotides
* Recognized by TATA-binding protein (TBP)
* Part of the TFIID complex
* Directs RNA Polymerase II to the start site

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A child with ̑̑-thalassemia is found to have a mutation at the invariant GU sequence of an intron. Explain the molecular consequence on the resulting mRNA.
back:
* Splice site mutation
* Failure to recognize the 5' splice donor site
* Causes intron retention or exon skipping
* Produces non-functional or truncated ̑̑-globin protein

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Describe the specific types of transcription products generated by eukaryotic RNA Polymerase III.
back:
* Transfer RNA (tRNA)
* 5S Ribosomal RNA (rRNA)
* Small nuclear RNA (snRNA) such as U6
* Small nucleolar RNA (snoRNA)

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Distinguish between prokaryotes and eukaryotes regarding the spatial and temporal relationship between transcription and translation.
back:
* Prokaryotes: Coupled; translation begins during transcription due to lack of nuclear membrane
* Eukaryotes: Separated; transcription in nucleus, translation in cytoplasm
* Allows post-transcriptional processing in eukaryotes

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Identify the enzyme responsible for adding the poly-A tail to eukaryotic mRNA and the consensus signal sequence it recognizes.
back:
* Polyadenylate polymerase
* Recognizes the AAUAAA signal sequence
* Adds ~40-250 adenine nucleotides
* Aids in nuclear export and mRNA stability

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: In the eukaryotic nucleolus, the primary enzyme responsible for synthesizing the 28S, 18S, and 5.8S ribosomal RNA precursors is [___].
back: RNA Polymerase I. • Localized in the nucleolus. • Synthesizes a single 45S pre-rRNA transcript. • Does not synthesize 5S rRNA (produced by Pol III).

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
coreConcept: Alpha-Amanitin Toxicity and RNA Polymerase II
front: A patient presents with fulminant hepatic failure after consuming wild mushrooms. The toxin involved, α-amanitin, lethally interferes with protein synthesis by inhibiting [___].
back: RNA Polymerase II. • Specifically inhibits messenger RNA (mRNA) synthesis. • Prevents the transcription of protein-coding genes. • Leads to cell death due to lack of essential mRNA templates.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast the number and location of replication origins found in prokaryotic DNA versus eukaryotic linear chromosomes.
back: • Prokaryotes: Single unique origin of replication (oriC). • Eukaryotes: Multiple origins per chromosome. • Eukaryotic multiplicity ensures rapid replication of massive linear genomes during the S-phase.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast the sensitivity of the three eukaryotic nuclear RNA polymerases to the fungal toxin α-amanitin in a clinical poisoning case.
back: • RNA Pol II: Highly sensitive; inhibited by very low concentrations. • RNA Pol III: Moderately sensitive; inhibited by high concentrations. • RNA Pol I: Insensitive. • Poisoning primarily results in a failure to produce mRNA.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Explain why eukaryotic transcription cannot occur simultaneously with translation, a process that is coupled in prokaryotes.
back: • Nuclear Membrane: Eukaryotes have a nuclear envelope separating the genome from ribosomes. • Spatial Separation: Transcription occurs in the nucleus, while translation occurs in the cytoplasm. • Temporal Separation: Eukaryotic pre-mRNA requires processing (capping, splicing) before translation.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: The eukaryotic core promoter consensus sequence located approximately 25 nucleotides upstream of the transcription start site is the [___].
back: TATA (Hogness) box. • Recognized by TATA-binding protein (TBP). • Part of the TFIID complex. • Directs RNA Polymerase II to the correct start site (+1).

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A patient with β-thalassemia has a mutation in the invariant GU sequence at the start of an intron. Predict the effect on the resulting messenger RNA.
back: Splicing Failure. • Spliceosome cannot recognize the 5' donor site. • Leads to exon skipping or intron retention. • Results in a non-functional mRNA and severe protein deficiency.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Describe the unique mechanism eukaryotes utilize to replicate the terminal ends of linear chromosomes, a problem not faced by circular prokaryotic DNA.
back: Telomerase (Ribonucleoprotein). • Uses an internal RNA template to extend the 3' G-rich strand. • Prevents chromosome shortening (senescence). • Acts as an RNA-dependent DNA polymerase (reverse transcriptase).

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Distinguish between prokaryotic and eukaryotic mRNA regarding their coding capacity and structural modifications.
back: • Prokaryotic: Polycistronic (multiple genes/mRNA); lacks 5' cap and 3' tail. • Eukaryotic: Monocistronic (one gene/mRNA); contains 7-methylguanosine cap and poly-A tail. • Eukaryotic mRNA requires splicing of introns.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Name the specific trans-acting factor that first binds the TATA box to initiate the assembly of the eukaryotic transcription pre-initiation complex.
back: TFIID. • Consists of TATA-binding protein (TBP) and TAFs. • Recruits other general transcription factors (TFIIA, TFIIB, etc.). • Positions RNA Polymerase II at the promoter start site.

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Unlike the single origin of replication (oriC) found in prokaryotes, eukaryotic linear chromosomes initiate DNA synthesis at [___] to ensure rapid genome duplication.
back:
• Multiple origins of replication
• Multiple replication bubbles formed simultaneously
• Necessary for the significantly larger and complex eukaryotic genome

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A 35-year-old patient presents with severe hepatic failure after consuming wild Amanita phalloides mushrooms. The toxin α-amanitin specifically inhibits which eukaryotic enzyme?
back:
• RNA Polymerase II
• Stops mRNA synthesis and protein production
• Leads to massive cellular necrosis, particularly in the liver

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Explain the role of the DNA Polymerase α/primase complex during the initiation of eukaryotic DNA replication.
back:
• Synthesizes a short RNA primer (primase activity)
• Extends the primer with a short piece of DNA (polymerase activity)
• Later replaced by more processive polymerases (delta or epsilon)

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast the mechanism of RNA primer removal in eukaryotes with that of prokaryotic DNA Polymerase I.
back:
• Prokaryotes: DNA Pol I 5'→3' exonuclease activity
• Eukaryotes: RNase H and Flap Endonuclease 1 (FEN1)
• Eukaryotic DNA polymerases lack 5'→3' exonuclease activity

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Describe the functional role of the Proliferating Cell Nuclear Antigen (PCNA) in eukaryotic DNA synthesis.
back:
• Serves as a sliding DNA clamp
• Enhances the processivity of DNA Polymerases δ and ε
• Functional equivalent of the prokaryotic Pol III β-subunit

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: In eukaryotes, the specialized ribonucleoprotein that maintains linear chromosome ends by acting as a reverse transcriptase is [___].
back:
• Telomerase
• Contains TERC (RNA template) and TERT (protein)
• Extends the 3' end of the G-rich telomeric strand

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A child is diagnosed with β-thalassemia after a mutation is found to create a new 'cryptic' splice site. This defect primarily disrupts which specific eukaryotic post-transcriptional process?
back:
• Splicing of pre-mRNA
• Removal of introns and joining of exons
• Mediated by the spliceosome (snRNPs)

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: How do Histone Acetyltransferases (HATs) facilitate the initiation of eukaryotic transcription?
back:
• Acetylate lysine residues on histone tails
• Neutralizes positive charges on histones
• Relaxes nucleosome structure to allow DNA access

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Distinguish between the RNA Polymerase types in eukaryotes versus the single RNA Polymerase found in bacteria.
back:
• Prokaryotes: Single polymerase for all RNAs
• Eukaryotes: Pol I (rRNA), Pol II (mRNA), Pol III (tRNA/5S rRNA)
• Eukaryotic polymerases require general transcription factors to bind promoters

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Identify the structural modification at the 5' end of eukaryotic mRNA that is absent in prokaryotic polycistronic transcripts.
back:
• 7-methylguanosine cap
• Attached via an unusual 5'-to-5' triphosphate linkage
• Protects mRNA from degradation and aids translation initiation

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: In eukaryotic cells, the transcription of protein-coding genes into pre-mRNA is catalyzed by the enzyme [___].
back: • RNA Polymerase II • Synthesizes mRNA, snoRNA, and miRNA • Highly sensitive to inhibition by α-amanitin

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: A 35-year-old female presents with acute hepatic failure after consuming wild mushrooms found in a forest. Laboratory analysis indicates inhibited mRNA synthesis. This pathology is caused by a toxin targeting which eukaryotic enzyme?
back: • RNA Polymerase II • The toxin is α-amanitin (from Amanita phalloides) • Prevents the formation of the transcription initiation complex

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Explain the role of the TATA box and TATA-binding protein (TBP) in the initiation of eukaryotic transcription.
back: • TBP (part of TFIID) recognizes and binds the TATA box • Recruits RNA Polymerase II to the core promoter • Positions the polymerase at the +1 transcription start site

category: Illustrate the transcription in eukaryotes focusing on the differences between pro- and eukaryotic replication
front: Contrast the structural organization of prokaryotic and eukaryotic messenger RNA regarding the number of protein-coding regions (cistrons).
