category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast the target molecules identified by Southern, Northern, and Western blotting techniques.
back:
• Southern: DNA fragments
• Northern: RNA (specifically mRNA levels)
• Western: Proteins (using labeled antibodies)

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Specify the fundamental goal of the Human Genome Project (HGP) regarding the human haploid genome.
back:
• Sequence all 3 billion base pairs
• Identify all 20,000–25,000 protein-coding genes
• Provide a reference map for genetic disease research

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: In recombinant DNA technology, small circular extrachromosomal DNA molecules that serve as vectors for carrying foreign DNA into host bacteria are known as [___].
back:
• Plasmids
• Contain an origin of replication
• Usually carry antibiotic resistance genes for selection

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A 30-year-old male tests positive for HIV on an initial ELISA screen. The next high-yield step to confirm exposure by detecting specific viral antibodies against viral proteins is [___].
back:
• Western Blot
• Highly specific compared to ELISA
• Identifies individual viral proteins (e.g., gp120, p24)

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Describe the process of creating a complementary DNA (cDNA) library and its primary advantage over a genomic library.
back:
• mRNA is converted to DNA via Reverse Transcriptase
• Lacks introns and non-coding sequences
• Allows expression of eukaryotic proteins in prokaryotic hosts

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between the 'Sticky Ends' and 'Blunt Ends' produced by restriction endonucleases during DNA cleavage.
back:
• Sticky: Staggered cuts with single-stranded overhangs; facilitate re-annealing
• Blunt: Straight cuts across both strands; no overhangs; requires T4 ligase

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Define the characteristic DNA sequence structure recognized by most restriction endonucleases.
back:
• Palindromes
• 4–8 base pair sequences
• Identical 5'→3' sequence on both complementary strands

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: In Southern blotting, the fundamental process whereby a single-stranded labeled probe binds to its complementary target DNA sequence is termed [___].
back:
● Hybridization (or Annealing).
● Requires prior alkaline denaturation of dsDNA.
● Allows specific detection among millions of fragments.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A PCR analysis of a child with suspected Cystic Fibrosis reveals a DNA product exactly 3 base pairs shorter than the normal control. Explain the molecular basis of this finding.
back:
● ΔF508 mutation.
● Deletion of three nucleotides.
● Results in loss of one Phenylalanine residue.
● Causes misfolding and proteasomal degradation of CFTR.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Describe the specific biochemical events occurring during the 72°C phase of a standard Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) cycle.
back:
● Primer Extension.
● Heat-stable Taq polymerase adds dNTPs.
● Synthesis occurs in 5' to 3' direction.
● Polymerase starts from the 3'-OH end of annealed primers.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast a Genomic DNA library with a cDNA library regarding their genetic content and the enzyme required for the latter's synthesis.
back:
● Genomic: Contains total DNA (introns, exons, and promoters).
● cDNA: Contains only expressed sequences (exons).
● Enzyme: Reverse Transcriptase (uses mRNA as template).

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: How does the A-to-T mutation in codon 6 of the β-globin gene facilitate the direct diagnosis of Sickle Cell Anemia via RFLP?
back:
● Abolishes the MstII restriction site (CCTNAGG).
● Produces a longer DNA fragment (1.35 kb).
● Normal β-globin produces a shorter fragment (1.15 kb).

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: The small, circular, extrachromosomal DNA molecules used as vectors to amplify foreign DNA in prokaryotic host cells are called [___].
back:
● Plasmids.
● Contain an origin of replication (ori).
● Carry antibiotic resistance genes for selection.
● Possess unique restriction endonuclease sites.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A forensic scientist identifies a suspect by comparing the number of short tandemly repeated sequences at specific loci between a crime scene sample and the suspect's DNA.
back:
● DNA Fingerprinting (DNA Profiling).
● Utilizes VNTRs (Variable Number Tandem Repeats).
● Based on RFLP or PCR analysis of polymorphic loci.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain the mechanism used to identify a specific colony in a cDNA library when the DNA sequence is unknown but a specific antibody is available.
back:
● Use of an Expression Vector.
● Bacteria transcribe/translate the cDNA insert.
● Labeled antibodies bind to the expressed protein products.
● Identifies the specific colony containing the target gene.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between Southern, Northern, and Western blotting based on the target molecule analyzed in each technique.
back:
● Southern: Target is DNA.
● Northern: Target is RNA (mRNA levels).
● Western: Target is Protein (uses antibodies).

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify the specialized computer-based field essential for the organization, storage, and analysis of the massive data sets generated by the Human Genome Project.
back:
● Bioinformatics.
● Essential for genomics and proteomics.
● Links molecular biology with information technology.
● Enables the development of precision (personalized) medicine.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: In the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), the heat-stable enzyme [___] is used to synthesize new DNA strands because it remains functional during the high-temperature denaturation step.
back: * Taq Polymerase (from Thermus aquaticus). * Withstands temperatures near 95°C. * Automates the amplification process without requiring fresh enzyme in each cycle.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A fetus is screened for sickle cell anemia. DNA analysis shows a 1.35-kb fragment instead of the normal 1.15-kb fragment after MstII digestion. Identify the molecular change causing this result.
back: * Loss of a restriction site. * Single nucleotide substitution (A to T) in codon 6 of β-globin. * Abolishes MstII recognition (CCTNAGG). * Results in a longer DNA fragment.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain the biochemical utility of utilizing Reverse Transcriptase specifically during the construction of a cDNA library for protein production.
back: * Synthesizes DNA using mRNA as a template. * Creates DNA copies lacking non-coding introns. * Allows for the expression of eukaryotic genes in prokaryotic host cells.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast the target molecules and typical probes utilized in Southern blotting versus Northern blotting techniques.
back: * Southern: Detects DNA; uses DNA/RNA probes. * Northern: Detects mRNA (expression levels); uses DNA/RNA probes. * Both utilize gel electrophoresis followed by membrane transfer.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Describe how antibiotic resistance genes within a plasmid vector facilitate the selection of successfully transformed bacterial cells.
back: * Act as selectable markers. * Only bacteria containing the plasmid survive on antibiotic-enriched media. * Distinguishes transformed clones from those that failed to take up the vector.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: DNA sequencing using the Sanger method relies on [___], which lack a 3'-hydroxyl group and thus terminate chain elongation upon incorporation.
back: * Dideoxynucleoside triphosphates (ddNTPs). * Lack of 3'-OH prevents further phosphodiester bond formation. * Generates fragments of various lengths for sequence determination.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A forensic laboratory analyzes a biological sample from a crime scene. To establish a unique molecular profile, they analyze polymorphisms characterized by [___].
back: * Variable Number Tandem Repeats (VNTRs) or Short Tandem Repeats (STRs). * Variations in repeat units are unique to individuals. * Detected via PCR or RFLP analysis.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain the primary goal of the Human Genome Project and its impact on the identification of genetic diseases.
back: * Determined the sequence of 3 billion base pairs. * Created a reference for identifying mutations and SNPs. * Facilitates Genome-Wide Association Studies (GWAS) to link alleles to diseases.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between a genomic library and a cDNA library regarding their sequence content and tissue specificity.
back: * Genomic: Entire genome (introns/exons); identical across tissues. * cDNA: Expressed sequences only (mRNA copies); tissue-specific. * cDNA is preferred for expressing eukaryotic proteins in bacteria.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify the primary molecule used as a probe in Western blotting to detect a specific protein after membrane transfer.
back: * Labeled antibodies (primary or secondary). * Bind specifically to target protein antigens. * Visualized through enzyme-linked reactions or fluorescence.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: In the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), the step where heat-stable DNA polymerase synthesizes a new strand at 72°C by adding nucleotides to the 3' end of the primer is called [___].
back:
• Extension (or Elongation) phase.
• Uses Taq polymerase (from Thermus aquaticus).
• Requires dNTPs and specific flanking primers to bracket the target sequence.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A prenatal screening for Sickle Cell Anemia shows a 1.35-kb DNA fragment instead of the normal 1.15-kb fragment upon MstII restriction digestion. Explain the molecular basis for this finding.
back:
• A-to-T point mutation in codon 6 of the β-globin gene.
• Abolishes the MstII recognition site (CCTNAGG).
• Results in a longer RFLP fragment due to the loss of a cleavage site.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain the mechanistic role of dideoxynucleotide triphosphates (ddNTPs) in Sanger DNA sequencing.
back:
• ddNTPs lack a 3'-hydroxyl group (3'-OH).
• Their incorporation prevents the formation of a 3'-to-5' phosphodiester bond.
• Causes sequence-specific chain termination during DNA synthesis.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast Southern, Northern, and Western blotting regarding the specific macromolecule they detect and the probe used.
back:
• Southern: Detects DNA using a DNA/RNA probe.
• Northern: Detects mRNA using a DNA/RNA probe.
• Western: Detects Protein using labeled Antibodies.
• All utilize gel electrophoresis for size separation.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: List three essential characteristics required for a DNA molecule to serve as an effective cloning vector.
back:
• Autonomous replication (Origin of replication).
• Selectable marker (e.g., Antibiotic resistance gene).
• Unique restriction enzyme recognition sites (Multiple Cloning Site).

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: The primary objective of the Human Genome Project was to determine the sequence of approximately [___] billion base pairs that make up the haploid human genome.
back:
• 3 billion base pairs.
• Identified 20,000–25,000 protein-coding genes.
• Completed in 2003, providing a reference for genetic disease mapping.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: In a family with Phenylketonuria (PKU), an RFLP marker is found to be 'tightly linked' to the PAH gene mutation. How is this marker used for indirect prenatal diagnosis?
back:
• The marker and mutation are coinherited due to proximity.
• Southern blotting traces the marker's presence in the fetus.
• Identifies the mutant allele without knowing the specific molecular defect.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Describe the procedure of creating recombinant DNA during the molecular cloning of a human gene into a bacterial plasmid.
back:
• Digest human DNA and plasmid with the same restriction enzyme.
• Anneal complementary 'sticky ends' of both fragments.
• Apply DNA ligase to covalently seal the phosphodiester backbone.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between a Genomic Library and a cDNA Library regarding their content and the presence of non-coding sequences.
back:
• Genomic: Represents entire genome; includes introns, promoters, and intergenic regions.
• cDNA: Represents only expressed mRNA; lacks introns and control regions.
• cDNA requires reverse transcriptase and is tissue-specific.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Define the role of Variable Number Tandem Repeats (VNTRs) in forensic DNA profiling.
back:
• Short DNA sequences repeated one after another.
• Repeat count is unique to each individual (molecular fingerprint).
• Fragments are separated by size to distinguish between individuals.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: In the Southern blotting technique, specific DNA fragments are identified by hybridization with a labeled [___] that is complementary to the target sequence.
back:
* Single-stranded DNA or RNA probe
* Hybridizes via complementary base pairing
* Labeled with radioisotopes (32P) or fluorescent dyes
* Detects presence/size of specific genomic fragments

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A clinician needs to distinguish between a homozygous mutant and a heterozygous carrier of the sickle cell mutation using a rapid amplification method. The diagnostic test used is [___].
back:
* Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR)
* Amplifies target β-globin gene region
* PCR products are analyzed by size or hybridization
* Faster and more sensitive than biological cloning

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain the biochemical reason why the incorporation of a dideoxynucleotide (ddNTP) terminates DNA chain elongation during Sanger sequencing.
back:
* Lacks a 3'-hydroxyl (-OH) group on the sugar
* Prevents formation of the next 3' to 5' phosphodiester bond
* DNA polymerase cannot add subsequent nucleotides
* Results in fragments of varying lengths for analysis

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast a cDNA library with a genomic DNA library regarding the presence of non-coding regions and tissue specificity.
back:
* Genomic Library: Contains introns/regulatory sequences; identical for all tissues
* cDNA Library: Lacks introns; represents only expressed mRNA
* cDNA Library: Varies significantly between different cell types/environmental conditions

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Describe the underlying principle of Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism (RFLP) in tracing genetic mutations.
back:
* DNA variations (SNPs) alter restriction endonuclease sites
* Mutations create or abolish specific cleavage points
* Digestion produces fragments of differing lengths
* Fragments are separated by electrophoresis for genotype identification

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A [___] is a small, circular, extrachromosomal DNA molecule used in recombinant DNA technology to amplify foreign DNA within a host bacterium.
back:
* Plasmid
* Capable of autonomous replication
* Contains at least one unique restriction site
* Carries antibiotic resistance genes for selective growth

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A researcher observes that a patient with a suspected urea cycle defect has a normal-length OTC mRNA on a Northern blot but zero enzyme activity. This suggests the defect lies in [___].
back:
* Translation or post-translational modification
* Gene is transcribed into mRNA successfully
* Northern blot confirms mRNA size/presence
* Protein synthesis or folding is likely impaired

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Describe the specific temperature-dependent steps of a single PCR cycle and their biological purposes.
back:
* Denaturation (95°C): Separates double-stranded DNA
* Annealing (50-60°C): Primers bind to flanking sequences
* Extension (72°C): Heat-stable Taq polymerase synthesizes new strands
* Cycle repeats 20-30 times for exponential amplification

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between Western blotting and Southern blotting based on the target molecule and the detection tool used.
back:
* Southern Blot: Targets DNA; uses labeled nucleic acid probes
* Western Blot: Targets Protein; uses labeled antibodies
* Both utilize electrophoresis for size-based separation
* Western detects post-translational modifications or abundance

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify the characteristic symmetry of DNA sequences recognized and cleaved by restriction endonucleases.
back:
* Palindromes (twofold rotational symmetry)
* Sequence reads the same 5' to 3' on both strands
* Examples include EcoRI (GAATTC) and HindIII
* Allows precise cleavage into manageable restriction fragments

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: The heat-stable DNA polymerase derived from *Thermus aquaticus* used in PCR to synthesize new DNA strands at high temperatures is [___].
back:
* **Taq Polymerase**
* Resists denaturation during high-temperature melting steps
* Facilitates automated, repetitive cycles of DNA amplification.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A Southern blot for Sickle Cell Anemia shows a 1.35 kb fragment instead of the normal 1.15 kb fragment when using the MstII enzyme. This change is caused by [___].
back:
* **Abolition of a restriction site**
* Point mutation (A to T) at codon 6 of the beta-globin gene
* Loss of the MstII recognition sequence results in a longer DNA fragment.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain the three essential properties required for a DNA molecule (e.g., a plasmid) to function as an effective cloning vector.
back:
* **Autonomous replication**: Origin of replication (ori) for independent synthesis
* **Selectable markers**: Antibiotic resistance genes for host cell selection
* **Restriction sites**: Unique sequences for inserting foreign DNA.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast Southern, Northern, and Western blotting regarding the specific target macromolecule and the type of probe utilized in each technique.
back:
* **Southern**: Detects DNA; uses DNA or RNA probes
* **Northern**: Detects mRNA; uses DNA or RNA probes
* **Western**: Detects Proteins; uses labeled Antibodies as probes.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: State the biochemical rationale for using dideoxynucleotides (ddNTPs) in the Sanger method of DNA sequencing.
back:
* **Chain termination**
* ddNTPs lack a **3'-hydroxyl group**
* Prevents the formation of the next 3'-to-5' phosphodiester bond, stopping elongation.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: The international collaborative effort completed in 2003 to determine the entire nucleotide sequence of the 3 billion base pairs in human DNA is the [___].
back:
* **Human Genome Project (HGP)**
* Identified approximately 20,000–25,000 protein-coding genes
* Provided a reference for identifying mutations and genetic diseases.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A PCR analysis for a neonate suspected of having Cystic Fibrosis reveals a DNA product 3 base pairs shorter than the normal control. Explain the specific molecular defect indicated.
back:
* **Three-base deletion (Delta-F508)**
* Results in the loss of one **Phenylalanine** residue
* Causes incorrect protein folding and subsequent proteasomal degradation.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Describe the specific role of Reverse Transcriptase in the construction of a complementary DNA (cDNA) library.
back:
* **RNA-directed DNA synthesis**
* Uses mRNA as a template to produce double-stranded DNA
* Allows for cloning of genes without non-coding introns.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between a Genomic DNA library and a cDNA library based on the presence of non-coding regions and tissue specificity.
back:
* **Genomic**: Entire genome including introns and promoters; same for all cells
* **cDNA**: Only expressed sequences (exons); varies by tissue and cell state.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify the characteristic nucleotide sequence arrangement (e.g., 5'-GAATTC-3') recognized and cleaved by restriction endonucleases.
back:
* **Palindromes**
* Sequences exhibit **twofold rotational symmetry**
* The sequence read 5'-to-3' is identical on both complementary strands.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Bacterial enzymes used in recombinant DNA technology that recognize specific 4–8 base pair palindromic sequences to produce sticky or blunt ends are [___].
back:
* Restriction endonucleases
* Form precisely defined restriction fragments
* Essential for inserting DNA into vectors
* Protect host bacteria from foreign DNA

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A couple undergoes prenatal screening for Sickle Cell Anemia. Analysis reveals the fetal DNA lacks a specific MstII cleavage site in the ̢-globin gene. Identify the likely diagnosis.
back:
* Sickle Cell Anemia (HbS)
* Point mutation (A to T) abolishes the MstII site
* RFLP generates a longer 1.35-kb fragment
* Confirmed by Southern blot or PCR

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain the molecular event occurring during the 50°C to 60°C phase of a standard Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) cycle.
back:
* Primer Annealing
* Synthetic primers bind to complementary flanking sequences
* Guides DNA polymerase to the target region
* Ensures specific amplification of the target DNA

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast the laboratory utility of Southern blotting with Northern blotting in a patient suspected of having a large genomic deletion versus a transcriptional regulatory defect.
back:
* Southern: Analyzes genomic DNA to detect deletions/mutations
* Northern: Analyzes mRNA to measure gene expression levels
* Southern: Uses DNA probes for genotype assessment
* Northern: Uses probes to determine transcript abundance

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify the essential structural feature of the nucleotides added to Sanger sequencing reaction tubes that causes premature termination of DNA chain elongation.
back:
* Dideoxynucleotides (ddNTPs)
* Absence of a 3'-hydroxyl (-OH) group
* Prevents formation of the next phosphodiester bond
* Results in fragments ending at specific bases

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A DNA library created using reverse transcriptase to copy processed mRNA into double-stranded DNA, which lacks introns and regulatory regions, is a [___].
back:
* cDNA (Complementary DNA) library
* Represents only expressed protein-coding genes
* Essential for expressing human proteins in bacteria
* Reflects tissue-specific gene expression

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A researcher compares fluorescently labeled cDNA from malignant breast tissue with normal tissue on a single slide containing thousands of DNA spots. Name this technique and its purpose.
back:
* DNA Microarray (Gene Chip)
* Evaluates global gene expression patterns simultaneously
* Identifies upregulated and downregulated gene subsets
* Used for tumor subclassification and personalized medicine

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Describe the specific enzymatic requirements for constructing a cDNA library that are not necessary for a standard genomic DNA library.
back:
* Reverse Transcriptase: Synthesizes DNA from mRNA template
* RNAse H or Alkali: Degrades the original RNA
* DNA Polymerase: Synthesizes the second DNA strand
* Genomic libraries only require restriction enzymes and ligase

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs) and Variable Number Tandem Repeats (VNTRs) as markers in RFLP analysis.
back:
* SNPs: Single base variations that alter restriction sites
* VNTRs: Variations in the number of repeated sequences
* SNPs: Most common form of genomic variation
* VNTRs: Primary tool for forensic molecular fingerprinting

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: State the primary goal and the year of completion for the Human Genome Project.
back:
* Goal: Sequence the 3 billion human base pairs
* Completed: 2003
* Identified: 20,000–25,000 protein-coding genes
* Enabled mapping of thousands of genetic disorders

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Restriction endonucleases recognize specific short stretches of double-stranded DNA (4-8 bp) that exhibit twofold rotational symmetry, known as [___].
back: - Palindromes. - The sequence reads the same 5′→3′ on both strands. - Examples include EcoRI and HaeIII which produce sticky or blunt ends.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
coreConcept: RFLP Diagnosis of Sickle Cell Anemia
front: A fetus is screened for sickle cell anemia using RFLP. DNA analysis shows a 1.35-kb fragment instead of the normal 1.15-kb fragment after MstII digestion. Identify the molecular basis for this finding.
back: - Point mutation (A→T) in codon 6 of β-globin. - Abolition/loss of an MstII restriction site. - Resulting fragment is longer due to missed cleavage.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Describe the specific temperature-dependent events occurring during the three phases of a single PCR cycle.
back: - Denaturation (95°C): Heat separates dsDNA into single strands. - Annealing (50°C): Primers bind to complementary flanking sequences. - Extension (72°C): Heat-stable Taq polymerase synthesizes new DNA 5'→3'.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast Southern, Northern, and Western blotting regarding the target molecule and the specific probe used for detection.
back: - Southern: Targets DNA; uses DNA/RNA probes. - Northern: Targets mRNA; uses DNA/RNA probes. - Western: Targets Proteins; uses labeled Antibodies.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain why the incorporation of a dideoxynucleoside triphosphate (ddNTP) terminates DNA chain elongation during Sanger sequencing.
back: - ddNTPs lack a 3′-hydroxyl (-OH) group. - This prevents the formation of a 3′→5′ phosphodiester bond. - DNA polymerase cannot add the next nucleotide to the chain.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: To clone a eukaryotic gene for protein expression in bacteria, the cDNA is inserted into a specialized plasmid containing a bacterial promoter and a [___] sequence for ribosome binding.
back: - Shine-Dalgarno (SD) sequence. - It is purine-rich and located 6-10 bases upstream of AUG. - It pairs with the 16S rRNA to initiate translation.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A patient's DNA is analyzed using radiolabeled allele-specific oligonucleotide (ASO) probes for the βS-globin mutation. If the DNA hybridizes with the mutant probe but not the normal probe, identify the clinical status.
back: - Homozygous for Sickle Cell Anemia (HbSS). - Both alleles contain the GAG→GTG point mutation. - Differentiates disease from sickle cell trait (heterozygous).

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain why a cDNA library is utilized instead of a genomic library when attempting to express human insulin in a prokaryotic host like E. coli.
back: - Prokaryotes lack the machinery to splice introns. - Genomic DNA contains non-coding introns. - cDNA is derived from mature mRNA and contains only exons (coding regions).

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between Southern blotting and DNA microarray analysis in terms of throughput and application.
back: - Southern Blot: Analyzes single/few gene fragments; low throughput. - Microarray: Analyzes thousands of genes simultaneously; high throughput. - Microarrays determine global gene expression patterns (genotyping/transcriptomics).

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify the total number of base pairs and the approximate number of protein-coding genes identified in the human genome by the Human Genome Project (HGP).
back: - 3 billion base pairs (haploid genome). - 20,000 to 25,000 protein-coding genes. - Completed in 2003 using automated Sanger sequencing.

category: Discuss the regulation of eukaryotic gene expression with special emphasis on iron metabolism and RNA interference
coreConcept: Iron Metabolism Regulation via mRNA Stability
front: In the regulation of iron uptake, the [___] mRNA is protected from degradation when Iron Regulatory Proteins (IRPs) bind to its 3'-untranslated region iron-responsive elements (IREs).
back: * Transferrin receptor (TfR). * Low iron levels trigger IRP binding. * Binding stabilizes the mRNA. * Increases receptor synthesis to maximize iron entry into the cell.

category: Discuss the regulation of eukaryotic gene expression with special emphasis on iron metabolism and RNA interference
coreConcept: Post-transcriptional RNA Editing of Apolipoprotein B
front: A patient is observed to have a full-length apolipoprotein B-100 in hepatic tissue but a truncated apolipoprotein B-48 in intestinal enterocytes. This tissue-specific protein variety is caused by [___].
back: * RNA Editing. * Post-transcriptional deamination of Cytosine to Uracil (C to U). * Changes a glutamine codon (CAA) to a stop codon (UAA). * Results in intestinal synthesis of the shorter B-48 protein.

category: Discuss the regulation of eukaryotic gene expression with special emphasis on iron metabolism and RNA interference
front: Explain the role of the RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC) in the physiological mechanism of RNA interference.
back: * Associating with a single-stranded microRNA (miRNA) guide. * Targeting complementary sequences in the 3'-UTR of specific mRNAs. * Silencing gene expression through either translational repression or endonuclease-mediated mRNA degradation.

category: Discuss the regulation of eukaryotic gene expression with special emphasis on iron metabolism and RNA interference
front: A patient exhibits elevated intracellular iron stores. Contrast the binding status of Iron Regulatory Proteins (IRPs) on Ferritin mRNA versus Transferrin Receptor (TfR) mRNA in this state.
back: * IRPs dissociate from both transcripts. * Ferritin: Loss of 5'-UTR binding allows translation for iron storage. * TfR: Loss of 3'-UTR binding leads to mRNA degradation, reducing iron uptake.

category: Discuss the regulation of eukaryotic gene expression with special emphasis on iron metabolism and RNA interference
front: Identify the specific structural motif used by trans-acting nuclear receptors, such as the estrogen or glucocorticoid receptors, to bind their respective response elements in DNA.
back: * Zinc finger motif. * Coordinated by zinc ions and cysteine/histidine residues. * Allows specific insertion of the protein into the major groove of the DNA double helix.

category: Discuss the regulation of eukaryotic gene expression with special emphasis on iron metabolism and RNA interference
front: During the maturation of microRNA (miRNA), the cytoplasmic endonuclease responsible for cleaving the pre-miRNA hairpin into a ~22-nucleotide double-stranded mature fragment is [___].
back: * Dicer. * A ribonuclease III enzyme. * Processes pre-miRNA after its export from the nucleus. * Generates the double-stranded precursor for the RISC guide strand.

category: Discuss the regulation of eukaryotic gene expression with special emphasis on iron metabolism and RNA interference
coreConcept: Regulation of Translation Initiation via eIF-2
front: A laboratory model of viral infection shows a rapid halt in global protein synthesis via the phosphorylation of an initiation factor. Identify this factor and the step it inhibits.
back: * eIF-2 (Eukaryotic Initiation Factor 2). * Phosphorylation prevents GDP-GTP exchange. * Inhibits the recycling of the initiation factor. * Prevents the formation of the translation initiation complex.

category: Discuss the regulation of eukaryotic gene expression with special emphasis on iron metabolism and RNA interference
front: Describe the molecular mechanism by which steroid hormone-receptor complexes overcome chromatin condensation to activate transcription after ligand binding.
back: * Hormone-receptor complex dimerizes and binds to Hormone Response Elements (HRE). * Recruits coactivators with histone acetyltransferase (HAT) activity. * Acetylation reduces histone-DNA affinity. * Decondenses chromatin to allow RNA polymerase access to the promoter.

category: Discuss the regulation of eukaryotic gene expression with special emphasis on iron metabolism and RNA interference
front: Distinguish the coordinate regulation of bacterial genes in an operon from the coordinate regulation of eukaryotic genes in a hormone response system.
back: * Prokaryotes: Related genes are clustered and transcribed into a single polycistronic mRNA. * Eukaryotes: Dispersed genes share common cis-acting response elements (e.g., HREs) recognized by the same trans-acting factor.

category: Discuss the regulation of eukaryotic gene expression with special emphasis on iron metabolism and RNA interference
front: What is the primary difference in origin between endogenous microRNA (miRNA) and exogenous small interfering RNA (siRNA)?
back: * miRNA: Endogenous, transcribed from the cell's own genome as pri-miRNA. * siRNA: Exogenous, typically synthetic double-stranded RNA introduced for therapeutic or experimental gene silencing.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: In the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), the heat-stable enzyme [___] is utilized to synthesize new DNA strands at high temperatures without being denatured during the process.
back:
- Taq Polymerase.
- Derived from the bacterium Thermus aquaticus.
- Essential for automating the extension phase at 72°C.
- Adds deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates (dNTPs) to the 3'-hydroxyl end of primers.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
coreConcept: RFLP Diagnosis of Sickle Cell Anemia
front: A neonate is screened for sickle cell anemia. Fetal DNA is digested with MstII, and Southern blotting reveals a single 1.35-kb fragment instead of the normal 1.15-kb fragment. This indicates [___].
back:
- Homozygous Sickle Cell Anemia (HbSS).
- The A-to-T mutation at codon 6 abolishes a restriction site.
- Loss of the MstII site results in a longer DNA fragment.
- Diagnostic of the βS-globin genotype.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain how the incorporation of dideoxynucleoside triphosphates (ddNTPs) enables the determination of a DNA sequence in the Sanger method.
back:
- ddNTPs lack a 3'-hydroxyl group required for bond formation.
- Incorporation prevents further 3'-to-5' phosphodiester linkage.
- Chain elongation terminates at specific nucleotide bases.
- Resulting fragments are separated by electrophoresis to read the sequence.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast the function of a Primer in PCR with that of a Probe in Southern blotting.
back:
- Primer: Short oligonucleotide providing a 3'-OH end for DNA polymerase extension.
- Probe: Labeled single-stranded DNA/RNA used to detect specific sequences via hybridization.
- Primers initiate synthesis; Probes facilitate visualization of target fragments.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Describe the specific structural characteristic of the DNA sequences recognized and cleaved by restriction endonucleases.
back:
- Palindromes (Twofold rotational symmetry).
- The 5'→3' sequence is identical on both strands.
- Recognition sites typically range from 4 to 8 base pairs.
- Cleavage generates either cohesive (sticky) or blunt ends.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: To confirm a positive HIV ELISA result by detecting specific viral proteins like p24 or gp120 in a patient's serum, the [___] technique is employed.
back:
- Western Blotting (Immunoblotting).
- Involves separation of proteins by electrophoresis.
- Utilizes labeled antibodies as probes to detect specific antigens.
- Provides a highly specific confirmatory test for HIV exposure.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A family with a history of Phenylketonuria (PKU) undergoes prenatal testing. If the disease-causing mutation does not directly alter a restriction site, the condition can still be traced using [___].
back:
- Indirect RFLP analysis via Linkage.
- Relies on polymorphisms (SNP or VNTR) closely linked to the PAH gene.
- The polymorphism acts as a marker for the defective allele.
- Requires DNA from affected family members for comparison.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Describe the three distinct temperature-dependent steps of a single Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) cycle.
back:
- Denaturation (95°C): High heat separates double-stranded DNA into single strands.
- Annealing (50°C): Primers bind to complementary flanking sequences.
- Extension (72°C): Taq polymerase synthesizes new DNA strands from the 3'-ends.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between Southern blotting and Northern blotting based on the target molecule and purpose.
back:
- Southern Blot: Targets DNA; used to detect mutations, insertions, or deletions.
- Northern Blot: Targets mRNA; used to measure gene expression levels and size.
- Both utilize electrophoresis and labeled nucleic acid probes for hybridization.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify the primary outcome and genomic scale of the Human Genome Project (HGP) completed in 2003.
back:
- Sequenced all 3 billion base pairs of the human genome.
- Identified approximately 20,000 to 25,000 protein-coding genes.
- Provided a reference map for detecting mutations.
- Enabled advances in personalized medicine and genomic research.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: The heat-stable enzyme [___], isolated from Thermus aquaticus, is essential for the extension phase of the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR).
back:
Taq Polymerase. 

*   Functions at high temperatures (approx. 72°C). 
*   Lacks 3'→5' exonuclease activity (proofreading). 
*   Synthesizes DNA in the 5'→3' direction.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
coreConcept: RFLP Application in Sickle Cell Anemia
front: A fetus is screened for sickle cell anemia using RFLP. This diagnosis is possible because the A-to-T point mutation at codon 6 of the ̢-globin gene abolishes a recognition site for the enzyme [___].
back:
MstII. 

*   Normal gene yields a 1.15-kb fragment. 
*   Mutant ̢S gene yields a 1.35-kb fragment due to loss of a cleavage site. 
*   Detected via Southern blotting and hybridization.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain the three essential structural features required for a DNA molecule to serve as an effective cloning vector.
back:
*   Origin of Replication: Allows autonomous replication within the host cell. 
*   Selectable Marker: Usually an antibiotic resistance gene (e.g., ampicillin) for identifying successful transformants. 
*   Restriction Sites: Unique sequences for inserting foreign DNA fragments.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast the structural content of a genomic DNA library with that of a cDNA library regarding non-coding regions.
back:
*   Genomic Library: Contains the entire genome, including introns, promoters, and intergenic regions. 
*   cDNA Library: Derived from mRNA; contains only exons (protein-coding sequences) and lacks introns/regulatory elements.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Specify the unique characteristic of the nucleotide substrate that causes chain termination in the Sanger sequencing method.
back:
Dideoxynucleoside triphosphates (ddNTPs). 

*   They lack a 3'-hydroxyl group on the sugar moiety. 
*   Prevention of phosphodiester bond formation with the next incoming nucleotide stops elongation.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: The blotting technique used to measure the size and abundance of specific mRNA molecules in a sample using a labeled probe is [___].
back:
Northern Blotting. 

*   Involves electrophoresis of RNA. 
*   Transfer to a nitrocellulose/nylon membrane. 
*   Hybridization with a complementary DNA or RNA probe.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A newborn of an HIV-positive mother requires testing. Explain why PCR-based testing is preferred over ELISA in the first few months of life.
back:
*   Direct Detection: PCR identifies viral nucleic acids directly. 
*   ELISA Limitation: Maternal IgG antibodies can persist in the infant, giving a false positive. 
*   Window Period: PCR can detect the virus before the infant's immune system produces its own antibodies.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
coreConcept: Human Genome Project and Exome Analysis
front: Describe the focus of "Exome Sequencing" as an advancement in biotechnology following the Human Genome Project.
back:
*   Target: Sequences only the protein-coding regions (exons). 
*   Significance: Covers ~1-2% of the genome but contains ~85% of known disease-causing mutations. 
*   Efficiency: Faster and more cost-effective than whole-genome sequencing.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between Southern blotting and Western blotting regarding their target molecules and probes.
back:
*   Southern Blot: Targets DNA; utilizes a labeled single-stranded DNA or RNA probe. 
*   Western Blot: Targets Proteins; utilizes labeled antibodies (primary and secondary) for detection.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify the characteristic symmetry found in the short DNA sequences recognized by restriction endonucleases.
back:
Palindromes (Two-fold rotational symmetry). 

*   The 5' to 3' sequence is identical on both strands. 
*   Examples: EcoRI (GAATTC) or HaeIII (GGCC). 
*   Allows enzymes to produce sticky or blunt ends.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: The thermostable enzyme commonly used in the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) to withstand high denaturation temperatures is [___].
back:
* Taq Polymerase
* Isolated from Thermus aquaticus
* Functions optimally at 72°C during extension
* Lacks 3' to 5' exonuclease proofreading activity

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A neonate is screened for sickle cell anemia. DNA analysis shows the loss of an MstII restriction site in the β-globin gene. Identify the molecular technique and the specific observation for a positive diagnosis.
back:
* Technique: RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism)
* Observation: 1.35 kb fragment (vs 1.15 kb normal)
* Cause: A-to-T mutation at codon 6 abolishes the cleavage site

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain the three repetitive steps involved in a single cycle of the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR).
back:
* Denaturation (95°C): Separates dsDNA into single strands
* Annealing (50°C): Primers bind to flanking sequences
* Extension (72°C): DNA polymerase synthesizes new strands 5' to 3'

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast Southern, Northern, and Western blotting based on the specific macromolecule they are designed to detect.
back:
* Southern: Detects DNA fragments
* Northern: Detects mRNA molecules
* Western: Detects specific proteins using labeled antibodies
* All three utilize gel electrophoresis and membrane transfer

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Describe the primary biochemical requirement for chain termination in the Sanger dideoxy sequencing method.
back:
* Incorporation of Dideoxynucleoside triphosphates (ddNTPs)
* ddNTPs lack a 3'-hydroxyl group
* Prevents formation of the next 3'-5' phosphodiester bond
* Results in DNA fragments of varying lengths

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: In recombinant DNA technology, a small, circular extrachromosomal DNA molecule used to carry foreign DNA into a host cell is called a [___].
back:
* Plasmid (Cloning Vector)
* Contains autonomous origin of replication
* Carries selectable markers like antibiotic resistance genes
* Possesses unique restriction endonuclease recognition sites

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A family with a history of Phenylketonuria (PKU) undergoes prenatal testing. If the specific mutation is unknown, how is RFLP used to determine the fetal status?
back:
* Indirect diagnosis via linkage analysis
* Traces polymorphic markers (SNP/VNTR) coinherited with the mutant PAH gene
* Requires DNA from an affected family member to identify the risk-associated allele

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Outline the mechanism by which a cDNA library is constructed from a tissue's total mRNA.
back:
* Reverse Transcriptase synthesizes DNA from mRNA template
* Oligo-dT primers bind the mRNA poly-A tail
* RNA is degraded, and DNA polymerase synthesizes the second strand
* Lacks introns and promoter regions

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between a genomic DNA library and a complementary DNA (cDNA) library regarding their genetic content.
back:
* Genomic: Contains entire genome (exons, introns, promoters)
* cDNA: Represents only expressed mRNA (no introns)
* cDNA library varies by tissue type; genomic library is constant

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify the characteristic symmetry found in the recognition sequences of restriction endonucleases.
back:
* Palindromic sequence
* Twofold rotational symmetry
* Sequence reads the same 5' to 3' on both complementary strands
* Examples include EcoRI and HaeIII

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: In the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), the heat-stable enzyme [___] is used to extend the primers by adding dNTPs in the 5' to 3' direction.
back:
* Taq Polymerase
* Derived from Thermus aquaticus
* Resists denaturation at high temperatures (95°C)
* Allows for repeated cycles of amplification

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
coreConcept: RFLP Diagnosis of Sickle Cell Anemia
front: A couple with a family history of sickle cell anemia undergoes prenatal screening. RFLP analysis shows a 1.35-kb fragment instead of the normal 1.15-kb fragment. This indicates the loss of a restriction site for which enzyme?
back:
* MstII restriction enzyme
* The A-to-T mutation in codon 6 of the β-globin gene abolishes this site
* The resulting longer fragment (1.35-kb) confirms the presence of the βS allele

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Describe the basic mechanism of biologic DNA cloning using a plasmid vector.
back:
* Restriction enzymes cut target DNA and plasmid at specific sites
* DNA ligase joins fragments to form recombinant DNA
* Transformation introduces the hybrid plasmid into host bacteria for replication

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast the target molecules and probes used in Southern, Northern, and Western blotting techniques.
back:
* Southern: DNA target, DNA/RNA probe
* Northern: RNA target, DNA/RNA probe
* Western: Protein target, Antibody probe
* Used to detect mutations, gene expression, and protein abundance respectively

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify the biochemical reason why the incorporation of a dideoxynucleoside triphosphate (ddNTP) terminates DNA chain elongation in Sanger sequencing.
back:
* ddNTPs lack a 3'-hydroxyl (-OH) group
* Prevents the formation of a 3'-to-5' phosphodiester bond
* No further nucleotides can be added to the growing strand

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
coreConcept: Human Genome Project and the Exome
front: The collection of all protein-coding sequences in the human genome, representing about 2% of the total DNA, is known as the [___].
back:
* Exome
* High-yield for identifying disease-causing mutations
* Target of high-throughput 'Exome Sequencing' in clinical genetics

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A patient suspected of early-stage HIV infection has a negative ELISA for antibodies. To directly detect the presence of the virus during this 'window period', which technique is used?
back:
* RT-PCR (Reverse Transcriptase-PCR)
* Converts viral RNA into cDNA then amplifies it
* Directly quantifies 'viral load' before seroconversion occurs

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain how Variable Number of Tandem Repeats (VNTRs) are utilized to create a DNA 'molecular fingerprint'.
back:
* Short DNA sequences repeated in tandem vary in number between individuals
* Restriction enzymes cut at flanking sites
