* Gel electrophoresis separates the fragments into a unique pattern

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between a genomic DNA library and a complementary DNA (cDNA) library regarding the presence of non-coding sequences.
back:
* Genomic Library: Contains total DNA including introns, exons, and promoters
* cDNA Library: Synthesized from mRNA via reverse transcriptase
* cDNA lacks introns and is used to express human proteins in bacteria

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Specify the defining characteristic of DNA sequences recognized by restriction endonucleases.
back:
* Palindromes (Twofold rotational symmetry)
* The sequence reads the same 5' to 3' on both complementary strands
* Usually 4 to 8 base pairs in length

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: In the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), the sample is heated to 95°C during the [___] stage to separate double-stranded DNA into single strands.
back:
● **Denaturation**
● High heat breaks hydrogen bonds between base pairs.
● Results in single-stranded DNA templates for the next cycle.
● Prepares DNA for primer annealing.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
coreConcept: RFLP Diagnosis of Sickle Cell Anemia
front: A fetus is screened for sickle cell anemia using RFLP. The loss of a specific restriction site for the enzyme [___] in the β-globin gene results in a 1.35-kb fragment instead of the normal 1.15-kb fragment.
back:
● **MstII**
● The A-to-T mutation in codon 6 abolishes the recognition site.
● Longer fragments indicate the presence of the βS allele.
● Differentiates between homozygous normal, trait, and disease.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain the specific chemical property of dideoxynucleotides (ddNTPs) that allows them to terminate DNA chain elongation in Sanger sequencing.
back:
● ddNTPs lack a **3'-hydroxyl (-OH) group**.
● DNA polymerase cannot form the next 3'-to-5' phosphodiester bond.
● This results in truncated DNA fragments of specific lengths for analysis.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast the targets and detection probes used in Southern blotting with those used in Northern blotting.
back:
● **Southern:** Targets DNA fragments; uses DNA or RNA probes.
● **Northern:** Targets mRNA molecules; used to measure gene expression.
● Both utilize electrophoresis and membrane transfer (blotting).

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify the three essential properties required for a DNA molecule to function as an effective cloning vector.
back:
● **Autonomous replication** within a host cell (origin of replication).
● Presence of unique **restriction sites** (multiple cloning site).
● At least one **selectable marker** (e.g., antibiotic resistance gene).

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: The specific portion of the human genome that encodes for proteins, representing only about 2% of the total 3 billion base pairs, is known as the [___].
back:
● **Exome**
● Focuses on expressed sequences (exons).
● Excludes non-coding introns and intergenic regions.
● High-throughput sequencing of the exome identifies most clinical mutations.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A newborn is suspected of having Cystic Fibrosis. PCR analysis of the CFTR gene reveals a product 3 base pairs shorter than the control. This indicates the presence of the [___] mutation.
back:
● **ΔF508 mutation**
● Represents a three-base deletion (CTT).
● Leads to the loss of a phenylalanine residue.
● Detectable by size differences in PCR products.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A researcher uses the pBR322 plasmid to clone a human gene. Explain how the presence of an antibiotic resistance gene allows for 'selection' of transformed bacteria.
back:
● Only bacteria taking up the plasmid survive on **antibiotic-containing media**.
● Non-transformed bacteria are killed.
● This ensures that every growing colony contains the recombinant DNA.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between 'Sticky ends' and 'Blunt ends' produced by restriction endonucleases during recombinant DNA synthesis.
back:
● **Sticky ends:** Staggered cuts leaving single-stranded overhangs; easier to ligate.
● **Blunt ends:** Straight cuts through both strands; no overhangs.
● Sticky ends are preferred for joining fragments from different sources.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify the primary goal and the year of completion for the international Human Genome Project.
back:
● **Goal:** Determine the complete nucleotide sequence of human DNA.
● **Completed:** 2003.
● Provided a reference for identifying genetic disease markers and SNP mapping.

• cDNA lacks introns/control elements.

front: How do restriction endonucleases distinguish between 'sticky ends' and 'blunt ends' during DNA cleavage?

• Blunt Ends: Straight cuts through both strands at the same position.
• Sticky ends facilitate easier ligation via complementary base pairing.

- Provides a 3'-OH start site for DNA polymerase.

- Highly polymorphic between individuals.

coreConcept: RFLP Diagnosis of Sickle Cell Anemia
front: A couple requests prenatal diagnosis for Sickle Cell Anemia. Analysis of the fetal β-globin gene via RFLP shows the loss of an MstII restriction site at codon 6. This mutation generates a larger DNA fragment of [___] kb instead of the normal 1.15 kb.
back:
1.35 kb
• Caused by A→T point mutation
• Abolishes the CCTNAGG recognition sequence
• Diagnostic marker for HbS allele.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain the biochemical basis for chain termination in the Sanger dideoxynucleotide method of DNA sequencing.
back:
• Incorporation of dideoxynucleoside triphosphates (ddNTPs)
• These lack a 3'-OH group on the sugar
• Prevents formation of the next 3'-to-5' phosphodiester bond.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast Southern blotting and Northern blotting regarding their target molecule and the necessity of DNA denaturation.
back:
• Southern: Detects specific DNA sequences; requires alkaline denaturation
• Northern: Detects specific mRNA; no denaturation needed (RNA is single-stranded).

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Briefly state why a cDNA library is preferred over a genomic library when the goal is to express a human protein (like Insulin) in an E. coli host.
back:
• cDNA is synthesized from processed mRNA
• It lacks introns (non-coding regions)
• Bacteria cannot splice eukaryotic introns.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: The Human Genome Project, completed in 2003, determined that the haploid human genome contains approximately [___] base pairs, only 2% of which encode proteins.
back:
3 billion (3 x 10^9)
• Distributed across 23 chromosomes
• Encodes approximately 20,000 to 25,000 genes.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A 30-year-old male tests positive for HIV antibodies on a primary ELISA screen. Identify the specific blotting technique and its probe used to confirm this diagnosis by detecting viral proteins.
back:
Western Blot
• Target: Viral proteins (e.g., p24, gp120)
• Probe: Enzyme-labeled antibodies
• Confirmatory test due to high specificity.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Outline the three thermal steps of a single PCR cycle and the physiological purpose of the highest temperature shift.
back:
• 95°C (Denaturation): Separates dsDNA into single strands
• 50-60°C (Annealing): Primers bind to flanking sequences
• 72°C (Extension): DNA synthesis by Taq polymerase.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between a Single Nucleotide Polymorphism (SNP) and a Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism (RFLP).
back:
• SNP: Variation at a single nucleotide (90% of genome variation)
• RFLP: Genetic variant that creates or abolishes a restriction site
• RFLP is the observable result of an SNP via gel electrophoresis.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: List the two most common types of DNA molecules used as 'cloning vectors' in recombinant DNA technology.
back:
• Bacterial Plasmids (circular extrachromosomal DNA)
• Viruses (e.g., Bacteriophage λ, Retroviruses)
• Both allow autonomous replication of foreign DNA inserts.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: The heat-stable DNA polymerase essential for the automated extension step of the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) is [___].
back:
- Taq Polymerase.
- Isolated from the bacterium Thermus aquaticus.
- Resists denaturation during high-temperature DNA melting cycles.
- Synthesizes complementary DNA strands in the 5' to 3' direction.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A neonate is screened for sickle cell anemia using MstII restriction enzyme. The presence of a 1.35-kb fragment instead of the normal 1.15-kb fragment on a Southern blot indicates the [___] of a restriction site.
back:
- Loss of a restriction site.
- Point mutation (A to T) at codon 6 of the ̢-globin gene.
- Eliminates the MstII cleavage sequence (CCTNAGG).
- Results in a longer DNA fragment during RFLP analysis.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Detail the essential biochemical steps required to produce a recombinant DNA molecule during molecular cloning in a bacterial host.
back:
- Cleavage of target DNA and vector with specific restriction endonucleases.
- Ligation of fragments into the vector using DNA ligase.
- Transformation of host cells with the hybrid plasmid.
- Selection of successful clones using antibiotic resistance markers.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A researcher uses a technique to identify a specific mutation in the Huntington gene by size-separating genomic DNA and using a radiolabeled probe. Identify the technique and the expected molecular finding.
back:
- Southern Blotting.
- Detection of an enlarged DNA fragment.
- Caused by trinucleotide repeat expansion (CAG) in the HTT gene.
- Uses hybridization to identify specific genomic sequences.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A patient with leukemia is treated with Cytarabine (araC). Explain the molecular mechanism by which this nucleoside analog inhibits DNA replication.
back:
- Incorporated into the growing DNA strand during S-phase.
- Modified sugar moiety prevents further chain elongation.
- Competes with natural deoxyribonucleotides for DNA polymerase.
- Halts the proliferation of rapidly dividing tumor cells.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: In the diagnostic procedure for sickle cell anemia, the restriction enzyme MstII is utilized to detect the mutation because it recognizes the specific palindromic sequence [___].
back:
- CCTNAGG.
- The A to T mutation in the ̢-globin gene abolishes this site.
- Generates a 1.35-kb fragment instead of a 1.15-kb fragment.
- Diagnostic for the sickle cell allele using RFLP.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A patient suspected of recent HIV exposure tests negative on ELISA but positive on a nucleic acid test. The technique used to detect viral load by quantifying copies of the target sequence after each cycle is [___].
back:
- Quantitative PCR (qPCR) or Real-time PCR.
- Quantifies target nucleic acids in real-time using fluorescent tags.
- Highly sensitive for early detection before antibody production.
- Directly detects viral DNA or RNA sequences.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A scientist is comparing a brain tissue sample with a muscle tissue sample to study expressed genes. Explain why a cDNA library is more appropriate than a genomic library for this investigation.
back:
- cDNA libraries reflect tissue-specific gene expression patterns.
- Derived from processed mRNA, thus excluding non-coding introns.
- Genomic libraries are identical for all somatic cells in an individual.
- Allows comparison of the active transcriptome between different tissues.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between the structural outcomes of DNA cleavage that result in 'sticky ends' versus 'blunt ends' produced by restriction endonucleases.
back:
- Sticky Ends: Staggered cuts creating single-stranded complementary overhanging regions.
- Blunt Ends: Straight cuts through both strands at the same position.
- Sticky ends facilitate more efficient ligation due to base pairing.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: State the primary objective of the Human Genome Project regarding the mapping of human DNA as completed in 2003.
back:
- To determine the entire nucleotide sequence of the human genome.
- Identified approximately 20,000 to 25,000 protein-coding genes.
- Mapped 3 billion base pairs across 23 chromosomes.
- Reference for identifying genetic variations and disease-causing mutations.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: In the Sanger method of DNA sequencing, the addition of [___] results in chain termination because they lack a 3'-hydroxyl group required for phosphodiester bond formation.
back:
● Dideoxynucleoside triphosphates (ddNTPs)
● They lack the 3'-OH group needed for DNA polymerase extension
● Resulting fragments are separated by size via electrophoresis to read the sequence.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
coreConcept: RFLP Diagnosis of Sickle Cell Anemia
front: A couple requesting prenatal diagnosis for sickle cell anemia undergoes fetal DNA analysis. The mutation abolishes the recognition site for the restriction enzyme [___], allowing direct detection via RFLP.
back:
● MstII
● The A-to-T mutation in codon 6 of the β-globin gene removes a cleavage site
● Produces a 1.35-kb fragment instead of the normal 1.15-kb fragment.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Describe the three temperature-dependent steps of a single Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) cycle.
back:
● Denaturation (95°C): Separates double-stranded DNA into single strands
● Annealing (50°C): Primers bind to complementary flanking sequences
● Extension (72°C): Heat-stable Taq polymerase synthesizes new DNA strands.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast a genomic DNA library with a cDNA library regarding their composition and presence of non-coding sequences.
back:
● Genomic: Total organismal DNA including introns and promoters
● cDNA: Derived from mRNA via reverse transcriptase
● cDNA lacks introns and can be used for bacterial protein expression.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify the essential properties a DNA molecule must possess to serve as an effective cloning vector.
back:
● Autonomous replication (Origin of replication)
● Unique restriction enzyme recognition sites
● Selectable markers, such as antibiotic resistance genes, for host cell selection.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: The technique used to detect specific protein products using labeled antibodies after electrophoretic separation and membrane transfer is known as [___].
back:
● Western Blotting (Immunoblotting)
● Uses specific antibodies as probes
● Determines the abundance, size, and post-translational modifications of targeted proteins.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: An oncologist uses a glass slide containing thousands of immobilized DNA sequences to analyze the global mRNA expression patterns of a patient's tumor. Identify this technology.
back:
● DNA Microarray (Gene Chip)
● Simultaneously measures mRNA levels for thousands of genes
● Useful for cancer subclassifying and precision (personalized) medicine.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain how RFLP is used for the indirect diagnosis of Phenylketonuria (PKU) when the specific mutation is unknown.
back:
● Uses polymorphic markers tightly linked to the PAH gene
● Traces the inheritance of these markers within an affected family
● Requires DNA from an affected relative to identify the marker-gene association.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs) and Variable Number Tandem Repeats (VNTRs) as markers for genetic variation.
back:
● SNP: Variation involving a single base pair (e.g., A to T)
● VNTR: Short DNA sequences repeated in tandem sequence
● VNTRs serve as unique 'molecular fingerprints' for forensic analysis.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Specify the unique characteristic of Taq polymerase that makes it indispensable for PCR.
back:
● Thermostability (Heat-stable)
● Isolated from Thermus aquaticus
● Does not denature during the 95°C heating phase of the PCR cycle.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: The primary heat-stable enzyme utilized in the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) to facilitate DNA synthesis at high temperatures is [___].
back:
*   Taq polymerase (from Thermus aquaticus).
*   Withstands 95°C denaturation temperatures.
*   Automates repeated amplification cycles without enzyme replenishment.
*   Lacks 3'→5' exonuclease proofreading activity.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A neonate at risk for Sickle Cell Anemia undergoes DNA analysis where a specific MstII restriction site is missing due to an A-to-T mutation. Identify this diagnostic technique.
back:
*   RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism).
*   Detects single-base changes that create or destroy restriction sites.
*   The ̢S mutation produces a 1.35-kb fragment instead of 1.15-kb.
*   Utilized for early prenatal diagnosis.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain the mechanical role of the 'blotting' step in Southern Blot analysis following gel electrophoresis.
back:
*   Transfers denatured single-stranded DNA from gel to nitrocellulose membrane.
*   Stabilizes fragments for hybridization with labeled probes.
*   Enables identification of specific sequences within a complex genomic digest.
*   Ensures the DNA remains accessible to large probe molecules.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast the composition and utility of a Genomic Library versus a cDNA (Complementary DNA) Library.
back:
*   Genomic: Contains entire genome including introns, promoters, and non-coding sequences.
*   cDNA: Represents only expressed mRNA; lacks introns and regulatory elements.
*   cDNA is preferred for expressing eukaryotic proteins in bacterial hosts.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Mention the specific functional purpose of incorporating 2',3'-dideoxynucleoside triphosphates (ddNTPs) during Sanger DNA sequencing.
back:
*   Act as DNA chain terminators.
*   Lack the 3'-hydroxyl group required for phosphodiester bond formation.
*   Generate fragments of varying lengths for size-based mapping of the sequence.
*   Essential for defining the terminal nucleotide of each fragment.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: In recombinant DNA technology, the small, extrachromosomal circular DNA molecules used as vectors to transport foreign DNA into bacterial hosts are [___].
back:
*   Plasmids.
*   Contain autonomous origins of replication.
*   Possess antibiotic resistance genes for selective screening.
*   Feature multiple unique restriction sites (polylinkers) for gene insertion.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A patient presenting with recurrent infections has a positive ELISA for HIV. Specify the laboratory technique used for confirmation by visualizing specific viral antigens.
back:
*   Western Blot (Immunoblotting).
*   Separates viral proteins by mass via electrophoresis.
*   Detects specific HIV antibodies against antigens like gp120 and p24.
*   Provides higher specificity than ELISA to prevent false positives.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain how RFLP enables the 'indirect' prenatal diagnosis of Phenylketonuria (PKU) when the causative mutation is not at a restriction site.
back:
*   Uses SNPs/markers tightly linked to the PAH gene.
*   Traces inheritance of the mutant chromosome within an affected family.
*   Requires DNA from an affected sibling (propositus) to establish linkage.
*   Utilizes linkage analysis rather than direct mutation detection.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between Southern Blotting and Northern Blotting regarding their primary target molecules and applications.
back:
*   Southern: Analyzes DNA; used for RFLP and gene structure.
*   Northern: Analyzes mRNA; used for assessing gene expression levels.
*   Southern requires DNA denaturation; Northern analyzes naturally single-stranded RNA.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify the unique structural characteristic of the 4-8 base pair DNA sequences recognized by restriction endonucleases.
back:
*   Palindromes.
*   Exhibit twofold rotational symmetry.
*   Sequence reads the same 5'→3' on both strands.
*   Allows enzymes to produce either sticky or blunt ends.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Bacterial enzymes that recognize and cleave double-stranded DNA at specific palindromic sequences, creating fragments for molecular analysis, are called [___].
back:
• Restriction endonucleases
• Recognize 4–8 base pair palindromes
• Produce either sticky or blunt ends
• Protect bacteria by restricting foreign DNA expression

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A fetus is screened for Sickle Cell Anemia using MstII restriction digestion. The loss of a cleavage site at codon 6 of the β-globin gene produces a 1.35-kb fragment instead of a 1.15-kb fragment, indicating a [___] mutation.
back:
• Single Nucleotide Polymorphism (SNP)
• Abolishes a specific restriction site
• Diagnostic for Hemoglobin S (HbS) allele
• Detected via Southern Blot or PCR-RFLP

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain the mechanical purpose of the 95°C heating step in a standard Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) cycle.
back:
• Denatures double-stranded DNA (dsDNA)
• Breaks hydrogen bonds between complementary bases
• Yields single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) templates
• Essential for subsequent primer annealing

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast a genomic DNA library with a cDNA library regarding their content and the presence of non-coding regions.
back:
• Genomic: Entire genome (introns and exons)
• cDNA: Only expressed mRNA sequences (exons only)
• cDNA: Requires reverse transcriptase for synthesis
• Genomic: Same in all cells of an organism

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify the specific structural feature of dideoxynucleotides (ddNTPs) that results in DNA chain termination during Sanger sequencing.
back:
• Lack of a 3'-hydroxyl (-OH) group
• Prevents formation of 3'-to-5' phosphodiester bonds
• Halts further nucleotide addition by DNA polymerase
• Allows size-based separation of fragments

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: The laboratory technique that utilizes gel electrophoresis followed by transfer to a membrane and hybridization with a DNA probe to detect specific gene sequences is [___] blotting.
back:
• Southern Blotting
• Detects DNA mutations (insertions/deletions/RFLPs)
• Requires DNA denaturation on the membrane
• Utilizes radiolabeled or fluorescent probes

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: An oncology researcher uses a glass slide containing thousands of immobilized DNA sequences to compare mRNA expression levels between healthy and cancerous tissues. This technology is a [___].
back:
• DNA Microarray (Gene Chip)
• Enables simultaneous analysis of thousands of genes
• Utilizes fluorescently labeled cDNA samples
• Facilitates personalized medicine and cancer subclassifying

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: How does a selectable marker, such as an ampicillin resistance gene, function within a plasmid vector during molecular cloning?
back:
• Permits survival of bacteria containing the plasmid
• Identifies successfully transformed host cells
• Inhibits growth of non-transformed bacteria
• Essential for isolating recombinant clones

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish Northern blotting from Western blotting based on the macromolecule analyzed and the probe used.
back:
• Northern: Analyzes mRNA using nucleic acid probes
• Western: Analyzes proteins using labeled antibodies
• Both: Use gel electrophoresis for size separation
• Western: Used as confirmatory test for HIV

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Specify the primary goal of the Human Genome Project regarding the mapping of genetic information.
back:
• Determine complete sequence of 3 billion base pairs
• Identify all human protein-coding genes
• Create a reference map for genetic disorders
• Completed in 2003 via high-throughput sequencing

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: The heat-stable DNA polymerase required for the extension phase of PCR, originally isolated from the bacterium Thermus aquaticus, is [___].
back:
• Taq Polymerase.
• It withstands high temperatures (95°C) during denaturation.
• It synthesizes DNA in the 5' to 3' direction.
• It lacks 3' to 5' exonuclease (proofreading) activity.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A prenatal screening for Sickle Cell Anemia using MstII restriction digestion reveals a 1.35-kb fragment instead of the normal 1.15-kb fragment. Explain the molecular basis of this finding.
back:
• Point mutation (A-to-T) in codon 6 of the β-globin gene.
• This mutation abolishes an MstII restriction site.
• Absence of cleavage results in a longer DNA fragment (1.35-kb).
• This is a classic diagnostic application of RFLP.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Describe the three mechanical steps of a single PCR cycle and their associated temperatures.
back:
• Denaturation (95°C): Hydrogen bonds break, separating dsDNA into single strands.
• Annealing (50°C): Synthetic primers bind to complementary flanking sequences.
• Extension (72°C): Taq polymerase adds dNTPs to the 3'-hydroxyl ends of primers.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast Southern, Northern, and Western blotting based on the target molecule detected and the specific probe utilized.
back:
• Southern: Detects DNA using labeled DNA/RNA probes.
• Northern: Detects mRNA using labeled DNA/RNA probes.
• Western: Detects proteins using labeled antibodies.
• All involve gel electrophoresis followed by membrane transfer (blotting).

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify three essential structural features required for a DNA molecule to serve as an effective cloning vector.
back:
• Origin of Replication: Allows autonomous replication in the host cell.
• Selectable Marker: Often an antibiotic resistance gene for host selection.
• Multiple Cloning Site: Contains unique restriction sequences for DNA insertion.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: The Sanger method, used extensively in the Human Genome Project, relies on the incorporation of [___] to terminate DNA chain growth.
back:
• Dideoxynucleoside triphosphates (ddNTPs).
• These molecules lack a 3'-hydroxyl group.
• Incorporation prevents formation of the next phosphodiester bond.
• This results in DNA fragments of varying lengths for sequencing.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A patient’s ELISA screen for HIV is positive. Describe the subsequent confirmatory test used and why it is preferred for diagnosis.
back:
• Western Blot.
• It separates viral proteins by size and identifies specific HIV antibodies.
• High specificity reduces false positives from ELISA.
• It is the gold-standard confirmatory test for antibody detection.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain the role of reverse transcriptase in the creation of a cDNA library and how this library differs from a genomic library.
back:
• Reverse transcriptase synthesizes DNA from an mRNA template.
• cDNA Library: Contains only expressed sequences (exons); lacks introns and promoters.
• Genomic Library: Contains the entire genome, including non-coding regions and introns.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between the two types of genetic variations that most commonly result in Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphisms (RFLPs).
back:
• Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs): Single-base changes that create or destroy restriction sites.
• Variable Number Tandem Repeats (VNTRs): Differences in the number of repeated sequences between restriction sites.
• Both lead to variations in fragment lengths.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify the primary mechanism bacteria use to prevent their own restriction endonucleases from cleaving their genomic DNA.
back:
• DNA Methylation.
• Methyltransferases add methyl groups to specific bases within restriction sites.
• Methylation masks the recognition sequence from the endonuclease.
• This allows the enzyme to selectively target foreign (non-methylated) DNA.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: The heat-stable enzyme isolated from Thermus aquaticus used in the extension phase of the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) is [___].
back: Taq Polymerase: 1. Heat-stable DNA polymerase. 2. Catalyzes 5' to 3' DNA synthesis. 3. Resists denaturation during high-temperature cycles.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A neonate is screened for sickle cell anemia. RFLP analysis shows a 1.35-kb fragment instead of the normal 1.15-kb fragment. This indicates the loss of a restriction site for the enzyme [___].
back: MstII: 1. Mutation (GAG to GTG) abolishes the MstII site. 2. Results in a longer DNA fragment. 3. Direct RFLP detection of the beta-S-globin gene.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain the primary biological principle behind the 'annealing' step in a PCR cycle.
back: 1. Cooling the reaction (approx. 50 degrees C). 2. Allows synthetic oligonucleotide primers to hybridize to flanking sequences. 3. Provides a 3'-OH end for DNA polymerase extension.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast a genomic DNA library with a cDNA library regarding the presence of non-coding sequences.
back: 1. Genomic Library: Contains total DNA including introns and promoters. 2. cDNA Library: Formed from mRNA; lacks introns and control elements. 3. cDNA represents only expressed genes.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify the specific structural feature of dideoxynucleotides (ddNTPs) that enables chain termination in Sanger sequencing.
back: 1. Lack of a 3'-hydroxyl (-OH) group on the sugar. 2. Prevents formation of the next 3'-5' phosphodiester bond. 3. Results in varying DNA fragment lengths.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: In molecular diagnostics, the technique used to identify specific DNA sequences by transferring electrophoresis-separated fragments to a membrane and hybridizing with a labeled probe is [___] blotting.
back: Southern Blotting: 1. Detects DNA mutations (insertions/deletions). 2. Identifies RFLP markers. 3. Uses radioactive or fluorescently labeled ssDNA probes.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A patient tests positive on an initial ELISA for HIV antibodies. Identify the 'Gold Standard' molecular technique used to confirm this diagnosis by detecting specific viral proteins.
back: Western Blotting: 1. Separates viral proteins by electrophoresis. 2. Blots to a membrane. 3. Uses labeled antibodies to confirm specific HIV proteins (gp120, p24).

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain the role of an 'expression vector' in recombinant DNA technology.
back: 1. Contains a bacterial promoter and Shine-Dalgarno sequence. 2. Allows for the transcription and translation of inserted cDNA. 3. Used to produce human proteins like insulin in bacteria.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between Southern and Northern blotting based on the macromolecule being analyzed.
back: 1. Southern: Analyzes DNA fragments for mutations. 2. Northern: Analyzes mRNA levels and size. 3. Both use gel electrophoresis and probe hybridization.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: State the characteristic symmetry of DNA sequences recognized and cleaved by restriction endonucleases.
back: Palindromes: 1. Sequence reads the same 5' to 3' on both strands. 2. Exhibits twofold rotational symmetry. 3. Example: EcoRI site (GAATTC).

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: In the Sanger method of DNA sequencing, the inclusion of [___] results in the termination of chain elongation because they lack a 3'-hydroxyl group.
back:
• Dideoxynucleotides (ddNTPs)
• The absence of a 3'-OH prevents further phosphodiester bond formation
• Results in fragments of varying lengths used to determine the exact nucleotide sequence.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
coreConcept: Direct RFLP Diagnosis of Sickle Cell Anemia
front: A couple with a family history of sickle cell anemia seeks prenatal diagnosis. Molecular analysis shows that the mutation in the β-globin gene abolishes a specific restriction site. Identify the endonuclease used for this RFLP analysis.
back:
• MstII restriction endonuclease
• The A-to-T mutation in codon 6 eliminates a cleavage site
• Normal DNA yields a 1.15-kb fragment; sickle cell DNA yields a 1.35-kb fragment.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain the role of synthetic oligonucleotide primers during the 'Annealing' phase of a Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) cycle.
back:
• Sample is cooled (approx. 50°C) to allow primers to bind target sequences
• Primers bracket the DNA region of interest
• Provide a free 3'-OH end for DNA polymerase to initiate elongation.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast Southern, Northern, and Western blotting based on the specific biological macromolecules they are designed to detect.
back:
• Southern Blot: Identifies specific DNA sequences using DNA/RNA probes
• Northern Blot: Analyzes RNA (mRNA) size and expression levels
• Western Blot: Detects specific proteins using labeled antibodies.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify the three essential structural features required for a DNA molecule to be utilized effectively as a cloning vector.
back:
• Capacity for autonomous replication within a host cell
• Presence of unique restriction endonuclease recognition sites
• Selectable markers, typically antibiotic resistance genes, to identify successfully transformed cells.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: The heat-stable enzyme [___] is the primary catalyst used in PCR to ensure DNA synthesis can continue after repeated high-temperature denaturation steps.
back:
• Taq Polymerase
• Isolated from the thermophilic bacterium Thermus aquaticus
• Remains stable at 95°C, eliminating the need to add fresh enzyme in each cycle.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A neonate is suspected of having Phenylketonuria (PKU). Because the specific mutation is unknown, indirect diagnosis is performed using RFLP. What requirement must be met for this linkage analysis to be successful?
back:
• Identification of genetic markers (polymorphisms) tightly linked to the PAH gene
• Determination of which marker is coinherited with the defective allele in that family
• Requires DNA from an affected family member for comparison.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain the mechanical role of Reverse Transcriptase in the creation of a cDNA library.
back:
• Synthesizes a DNA copy using messenger RNA (mRNA) as a template
• Converts single-stranded RNA into stable double-stranded DNA
• Allows the library to represent only the expressed genes of a specific tissue.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast a Genomic DNA Library with a cDNA Library regarding their content of introns and regulatory sequences.
back:
• Genomic Library: Contains total DNA, including introns and control regions
• cDNA Library: Contains only protein-coding sequences (exons) derived from mature mRNA
• cDNA lacks introns, making it ideal for bacterial protein expression.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: List the primary outcome and the total base-pair count identified by the Human Genome Project completed in 2003.
back:
• Determined the complete nucleotide sequence of the human genome
• Approximately 3 billion base pairs (10^9 bps)
• Identified roughly 20,000–25,000 protein-coding genes on 23 chromosomes.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: In the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), the heat-stable enzyme used to catalyze DNA synthesis during the extension step is [___].
back:
• Taq Polymerase
• Derived from Thermus aquaticus
• Resists denaturation at high temperatures (95°C)

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A prenatal test for sickle cell anemia utilizes the MstII restriction enzyme. The loss of a restriction site in the mutant β-globin gene results in a 1.35-kb fragment instead of the normal 1.15-kb fragment. Identify the technique used.
back:
• RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism)
• Detects point mutations (GAG → GTG)
• Abolishes specific MstII recognition site (CCTNAGG)

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain the primary objective and the procedural steps of a Northern blot.
back:
• Objective: Detects and quantifies specific mRNA sequences
• Steps: RNA electrophoresis → Transfer to membrane → Hybridization with labeled probe

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast a genomic DNA library with a complementary DNA (cDNA) library regarding the presence of non-coding sequences.
back:
• Genomic Library: Contains introns, promoters, and intergenic regions
• cDNA Library: Lacks introns and control regions; represents only expressed mRNA
• cDNA requires reverse transcriptase

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: List three essential properties required for a DNA molecule to function as a biological cloning vector.
back:
• Autonomous replication (Origin of replication)
• Unique restriction enzyme recognition sites
• Selectable marker (e.g., antibiotic resistance gene)

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: The [___] method of DNA sequencing utilizes dideoxynucleoside triphosphates (ddNTPs) to cause chain termination by lacking a 3'-hydroxyl group.
back:
• Sanger Dideoxy Method
• Chain termination at specific bases
• Fragments separated by size via electrophoresis

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A patient with suspected HIV requires quantification of viral RNA levels. Identify the specific modification of PCR used for this purpose and the enzyme required for the initial step.
back:
• RT-PCR (Reverse Transcriptase PCR)
• Enzyme: Reverse Transcriptase
• Converts viral RNA into cDNA before standard PCR amplification

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Describe how RFLP is utilized for the indirect diagnosis of an autosomal recessive disorder like Phenylketonuria (PKU) when the specific mutation is unknown.
back:
• Traces inheritance of polymorphic markers (SNPs/VNTRs)
• Requires a marker tightly linked to the disease gene
• Co-inherited within a specific family pedigree

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between Southern and Western blotting based on the target molecule and the type of probe utilized.
back:
• Southern: Targets DNA; uses labeled DNA/RNA probe
• Western: Targets Protein; uses labeled Antibody probe

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify the major scientific endeavor that mapped the 3 billion base pairs of human DNA and the approximate number of protein-coding genes identified.
back:
• Human Genome Project (HGP)
• Approximately 20,000–25,000 protein-coding genes
• Provides reference for identifying genetic disease mutations

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: In the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), the heat-stable enzyme typically used to extend the primers during the synthesis phase is [___].
back:
• Taq polymerase (from *Thermus aquaticus*).
• It functions optimally at high temperatures (72°C).
• It synthesizes the new DNA strand in the 5' to 3' direction.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A couple requesting prenatal diagnosis for sickle cell anemia undergoes fetal DNA analysis. The A-to-T mutation in the β-globin gene is found to abolish an MstII restriction site. This diagnostic approach represents [___].
back:
• Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism (RFLP).
• The loss of the restriction site results in a longer DNA fragment (1.35 kb).
• These fragments are visualized using Southern blotting.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Explain the biochemical mechanism by which dideoxynucleotides (ddNTPs) result in chain termination during DNA sequencing.
back:
• ddNTPs lack a 3'-hydroxyl (-OH) group.
• This group is essential for forming the next phosphodiester bond.
• Incorporation by DNA polymerase prevents further nucleotide addition.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Contrast Southern blotting and Northern blotting regarding their molecular targets and primary diagnostic utility.
back:
• Southern: Targets DNA; used to detect mutations like insertions or deletions.
• Northern: Targets mRNA; used to measure gene expression and transcript size.
• Both use electrophoresis and hybridization.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Identify the three essential structural features a plasmid must possess to serve as an effective cloning vector.
back:
• Origin of replication (for autonomous duplication).
• Selectable marker (e.g., antibiotic resistance gene).
• Unique restriction sites (multiple cloning sites for DNA insertion).

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: The international collaborative effort that sequenced the approximately 3 billion base pairs of human DNA and identified over 20,000 genes is the [___].
back:
• Human Genome Project (HGP).
• Completed in 2003.
• Established a reference sequence for mapping genetic diseases and variations.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: A patient with suspected early HIV infection tests negative for antibodies. To determine the 'viral load' directly by amplifying viral RNA, which specific technique is used?
back:
• RT-PCR (Reverse Transcriptase PCR).
• Converts viral RNA into cDNA before amplification.
• Highly sensitive for detecting viruses during the window period.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Describe the enzymatic steps required to synthesize a cDNA library from a pool of mature eukaryotic mRNA.
back:
• Reverse transcriptase synthesizes a DNA strand using mRNA as a template.
• Alkaline hydrolysis or RNase H removes the mRNA.
• DNA polymerase creates the second DNA strand.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Distinguish between a Genomic library and a cDNA library based on their nucleotide content.
back:
• Genomic: Contains all DNA including introns, exons, and promoters.
• cDNA: Contains only expressed sequences (exons).
• cDNA is derived from processed mRNA and lacks non-coding regions.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: Define the principle of 'hybridization' in the context of identifying specific DNA sequences using probes.
back:
• Annealing of a labeled single-stranded probe to its complementary target.
• Formed via specific hydrogen bonding (base pairing).
• Allows visualization of target fragments on a membrane.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
front: In the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), the heat-stable enzyme typically used to extend primers in the 5' to 3' direction is [___].
back:
• Taq polymerase (from Thermus aquaticus).
• Functions optimally at high temperatures (72°C).
• Lacks 3' to 5' exonuclease proofreading activity.
• Enables exponential amplification of specific DNA sequences.

category: Discuss the following Recombinant DNA techniques with reference to their principles, procedures and application: 1) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) 2) RFLP (Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism) 3) Cloning 4) Human Genome Project 5) Blotting Techniques 6) DNA (Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid) sequencing
coreConcept: RFLP Diagnosis of Sickle Cell Anemia
front: A 1-year-old child presents with anemia and dactylitis. Restriction analysis using MstII shows a 1.35-kb fragment instead of the normal 1.15-kb fragment. Identify the underlying molecular pathophysiology.
back:
• Sickle Cell Anemia (HbS).
• Point mutation (GAG to GTG) at codon 6 of beta-globin.
• Mutation abolishes a specific MstII restriction site.
• Results in a longer Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism (RFLP).

front: Explain the role of dideoxynucleoside triphosphates (ddNTPs) in the Sanger DNA sequencing method.
back:
• Act as specific chain terminators.
• Lack a 3'-hydroxyl group on the deoxyribose sugar.
• Prevent formation of the next 3' to 5' phosphodiester bond.
• Generate DNA fragments of varying lengths for electrophoresis.

front: A researcher needs to analyze a patient with a suspected collagen disorder. Contrast the utility of Southern, Northern, and Western blotting in this diagnostic workup.
back:
• Southern: Detects DNA mutations, deletions, or gene rearrangements.
• Northern: Measures mRNA levels, size, and tissue-specific expression.
• Western: Quantifies protein amount and post-translational modifications.
• All utilize gel electrophoresis followed by membrane immobilization.

front: Identify the three essential features a DNA molecule must possess to serve as an effective prokaryotic cloning vector.
back:
• Origin of replication for autonomous duplication.
• Selectable marker (e.g., antibiotic resistance gene).
• Unique restriction sites (Multiple Cloning Site) for DNA insertion.
• Ability to be easily isolated from host cells.

front: The landmark international effort to determine the complete nucleotide sequence of the 3 billion base pairs in the human genome is known as the [___].
back:
• Human Genome Project (HGP).
• Completed in 2003 with high-throughput sequencing.
• Identified approximately 20,000–25,000 protein-coding genes.
• Provided a reference map for identifying disease-causing mutations.

front: A newborn is suspected of having been exposed to HIV. Explain why PCR is preferred over ELISA for definitive diagnosis in the first few months of life.
back:
• PCR directly detects viral nucleic acids (DNA/RNA).
• ELISA detects anti-HIV antibodies, which may be maternal.
• Maternal IgG persists for months, yielding false positives.
• PCR provides sensitive detection during the window period.

front: Describe the specific nature of the DNA sequences recognized and cleaved by Type II restriction endonucleases.
back:
• Palindromic sequences (twofold rotational symmetry).
• Usually 4 to 8 base pairs in length.
• Sequence reads identically 5' to 3' on both strands.
• Cleavage produces either 'sticky' (cohesive) or 'blunt' ends.

front: Distinguish between a genomic DNA library and a complementary DNA (cDNA) library regarding their genetic composition.
back:
• Genomic: Contains all nuclear DNA (introns, exons, promoters).
• cDNA: Derived from mRNA via reverse transcriptase.
• cDNA lacks non-coding introns and regulatory sequences.
• cDNA library represents only expressed genes in specific tissues.

front: List the primary clinical utility of Allele-Specific Oligonucleotide (ASO) probes in medical genetics.
back:
• Detects known single-base mutations (SNPs).
• Identifies carriers (heterozygotes) for autosomal recessive disorders.
• Used in prenatal screening for CF and Sickle Cell.
• Requires prior knowledge of the specific mutation sequence.
